Effects.transfers: Applies to whoever owns this item

Chems.limitHint: Chems used today / chem limit (2 + half your Endurance modifier, min 1, max 4).
Chems.newDayHint: Roll the day over: charges hunger, dehydration and exhaustion for whatever the character went without (pg 119), resets the chem count, and clears effects still running.
Chems.newDayDone: Chem count reset for a new day.
Chems.newDayCleared: New day: chem count reset and {count} effect(s) worn off.
Chems.overdose: Over the chem limit ({used}/{limit}): gains {levels} levels of exhaustion (now {exhaustion}).
Chems.exhaustionLethal: Ten levels of exhaustion — the character dies (pg 136).
Chems.addictionFailed: Addiction check vs DC {dc} — addicted to {chem}
Chems.addicted: Addicted to {chem}. While not under its effects: {withdrawal} Clears after {weeks} week(s) without it.
Chems.noWithdrawal: (no withdrawal effect recorded on this item)
Chems.addictedTag: Already addicted — no further check on use.
Chems.recovery: Shaking an addiction takes {weeks} week(s) clean.

Roll.criticalFailure: Critical failure — the weapon gains a level of decay
Roll.outOfAmmo: {weapon} is out of ammo — reload first (6 AP)
Roll.reloadDecay: Reload #{interval} — {weapon} gains a level of decay
Roll.blindAttack: Blind attack at {distance} ft vs DC {dc}
Roll.blindHit: hit — a blind attack replaces the AC comparison, so this is the hit (pg 128)

Roll.blindBecauseBlinded: [You are blinded, so the attack with {weapon} is a blind attack (pg 128) — Luck replaces the skill bonus, and this DC replaces the target's AC.]
Roll.blindBecauseObscured: [The target is heavily obscured, so the attack with {weapon} is a blind attack (pg 128) — Luck replaces the skill bonus, and this DC replaces the target's AC.]
Roll.blindSprayAndPray: [Spray and Pray (pg 49) — advantage on the roll, and the DC is halved to {dc}]
Roll.sneakAttack: [SNEAK ATTACK — a critical hit if it beats their AC; hold Alt on the damage roll so it bypasses stamina]
Roll.sneakFromPosture: (sneak attack from your hidden position against an unaware target)
Roll.hiddenFromTarget: (advantage: you are hidden from this target)
Roll.targetDodging: (the target is dodging and can see you)

Rest.title: Rest
Rest.comfortable: Sleeping comfortably (a soft surface and shelter)
Rest.hint: One hour restores stamina; {long} hours also heal half your ability score + your level and remove a level of exhaustion. Without both a soft surface and shelter, the stamina and hit points regained are halved. {sleep}
Rest.hintShort: Rest. {long} hours heals and removes a level of exhaustion.
Rest.needsSleep: Sleeping stops the 24-hour exhaustion clock and ends the three sleep-cured diseases.
Rest.noSleep: This race does not require sleep, but still sheds exhaustion by resting.
Rest.radWorms: Rad worms bite in the night: {rads} level(s) of radiation.
Rest.tooShort: Too short to heal or shed exhaustion — that needs {hours} hours.
Rest.uncomfortableNothing: Resting rough halved the stamina back to nothing.
Rest.dayPassed: A day passes: +{hunger} hunger, +{dehydration} dehydration, +{exhaustion} exhaustion. Chem count reset, {effects} effect(s) worn off.
Rest.lethal: Ten levels of {condition} — the character dies.
Rest.inorganic: Inorganic body: no need to eat, drink, or sleep (pp. 8-9).
Rest.massExertion: Mass Exertion: a Super Mutant needs twice the food and water each day (pg 12).

Survival.title: Survival
Survival.irradiatedHint: Irradiated food gives one irradiated level; every {per} become a level of Rads (pg 83). The book never says whether the counter resets — a rolling counter is the only reading that converts more than once.
Survival.irradiatedConverted: Ten irradiated levels — one becomes a level of Rads, and the counter rolls over to {levels}.
Survival.irradiatedImmune: Evolution: no irradiated levels from food or water (pp. 8/11).
Survival.snackHint: A snack removes no hunger until you have eaten {needed} of them (pg 83). The book never says whether the pair must be the same snack, within what window, or how much hunger it removes — this counts any two, with no window, removing both baselines.
Survival.snackPaired: Two snacks together — {levels} level(s) of hunger removed.
Survival.stageHint: Buzzed: disadvantage on INT and PER, advantage on END and STR. Drunk adds -2 max AP and +level max SP. Hammered adds another +level SP and -5 on every d20 but Luck. Wasted adds a blackout and unconsciousness after an hour.
Survival.drinkBanked: That is {drinks} drink(s) toward the next stage.
Survival.alcoholAddicted: Addicted to alcoholic drinks: two levels of exhaustion at all times unless drunk. Clears after {weeks} week(s) off it.
Survival.addictedWarning: Alcohol addiction — two levels of exhaustion unless drunk (pg 82).
Survival.blackout: Wasted: no memory of any of this, and unconscious after an hour.
Survival.intakeHint: A day without one food costs a level of hunger; a day without three drinks (or one hydrating drink, marked *) costs three levels of dehydration; a day without sleep costs a level of exhaustion (pg 119, 133-134).

Repair.title: Repair {item}
Repair.bonus: Repair bonus from the Blueprint Encyclopedia
Repair.cannibalize: Use a copy or similar item (5 or fewer decay) as materials
Repair.hint: A Crafting check against 10 + the item's repair bonus (pg 93). Your Crafting bonus matching that value succeeds automatically. Failing costs half the time and half the materials but repairs nothing. Cannibalising a similar item repairs an extra level. Power Armor uses its own flat DC instead.
Repair.succeeded: {item} repaired: {levels} level(s) of decay off, now at {decay}.
Repair.failed: {item} not repaired — the Crafting check missed DC {dc}.
Repair.automatic: Crafting bonus meets the item's {bonus} — an automatic success, no roll needed.
Repair.failureCost: Half the time and half the materials are spent anyway (rounded down, which for most items is nothing).
Repair.brokenRestored: It was broken: back in service, but at {levels} levels of decay.
Repair.brokenCost: Repairing a broken item costs five times the time and materials, and raises the DC by {dc}.
Repair.cannibalized: The donor item is consumed; it must have had {max} or fewer levels of decay.
Repair.powerArmor: Power Armor: {minutes} minutes per level, plus 5 steel, 3 circuitry, 3 aluminum and 3 adhesive (pg 57).
Repair.materials: Materials come off the Blueprint Encyclopedia entry on this item.

Situations.title: Situations
Situations.syncHint: Turn every situational perk or trait on or off to match the situations that hold. Deliberately a button rather than automatic: nothing in this system writes documents on its own, which is what keeps it from racing Foundry's own updates.
Situations.derivedHint: The sheet works this one out from your own numbers — it cannot be toggled by hand.
Situations.declaredHint: Fiction the sheet cannot see. Click to declare it true or false.
Situations.noChange: Every situational effect already matches the situations that hold.
Situations.synced: Situational effects updated — switched on: {on}. Switched off: {off}.

Keywords.burstHint: Automatic fire (pg 69): the paid attack plus its free extra shots. Each extra shot must target something within 10 feet of the previous target, and drops the Agility modifier from its damage. One round is consumed per shot — the book never says so, but nothing else in it reads any other way.
Keywords.burstHeader: Automatic fire — {weapon}: {shots} attacks in all ({extra} of them free). Each extra shot must target a creature within {feet} ft of the previous one.
Keywords.burstShotKeepsMod: [extra shot {shot} — keeps its {ability} modifier: Automatic suppresses Agility only, and this weapon does not use it]
Keywords.burstDry: The magazine runs dry after {fired} extra shot(s) — the burst stops there.
Keywords.notAutomatic: This weapon has no Automatic: N property.
Keywords.spread: [Spread — in the second range increment this also hits everything within {feet} ft of the target; the book never says how those hits resolve, so that is the GM's call]
Keywords.semiAutomatic: Semi-Automatic: two paid attacks with this weapon in a row on your turn grant a third free (pg 70). Not automated — nothing here tracks AP spending yet.
Keywords.oneHandedMelee: [one-handed with a Two Handed weapon — disadvantage unless you spend {ap} extra AP]
Keywords.oneHandedRanged: [one-handed with a Two Handed ranged weapon — spend {ap} extra AP, or take this disadvantage and fall prone after attacking]
Keywords.oneHandedExempt: [one-handed, but Strength beats the requirement by {margin}+ — no penalty]
Keywords.unwieldy: [Unwieldy — one hand with a Perception score under {score}: disadvantage, and no AP buys it off]
Keywords.unwieldyExempt: [Unwieldy, but a Perception score of {score} carries it one-handed — no penalty]
Keywords.dismember: [Dismember — arms and legs cost no additional AP with this weapon]
Keywords.corrosive: [Corrosive — if this reaches their hit points, their armor gains a level of decay; Power Armor is unaffected]
Keywords.twoHandedHint: Two Handed costs nothing held properly. In one hand: melee takes disadvantage unless you pay 2 extra AP; ranged demands the 2 AP or you take disadvantage and fall prone. Either way, Strength 3 or more above the requirement waives it. The book never says a Two Handed weapon occupies two hands, so this is your declaration, not the weapon's.
Keywords.reloadHint: Reload costs {ap}. The weapon decays every {every} reloads. v2.1 also requires a free hand to reload (pg 66, 127) — the book gives nothing to check that against, so it is not enforced.
Keywords.manualHint: Manual Reload loads one round per AP spent, minimum {min} AP (pg 70). This magazine needs {needed} more. Note the minimum can exceed a small magazine's capacity — the book neither forbids that nor refunds the difference.
Keywords.speedloaderCheaper: A Speedloader (pg 76) fills this magazine for {ap} AP — cheaper than the {printed} AP just reported. AP is never deducted here, so tell the GM which one you spent.
Keywords.switchHint: Automatic (Switch): two modes of fire, {ap} AP to change between them (pg 69). Single shot and automatic carry different properties, and only automatic can burst.
Keywords.manualWasted: {ap} AP over what the magazine could take — the book gives no refund.

Block.description: +{dt} damage threshold against melee attacks, until you attack again.
Block.started: Blocks with {weapon} ({ap} AP) — +{dt} damage threshold against melee attacks until they next attack.
Block.ended: Lowers their guard — the block ends.
Block.already: Already blocking. Attacking ends it, or press Block again to lower your guard.
Block.needsMelee: Blocking needs a melee weapon in hand — equip one first. (v2.1 removed unarmed blocking.)
Block.hint: 3 AP. Grants +2 + your Endurance modifier to damage threshold against melee attacks, and lasts until you attack again rather than for a set time.
Block.active: Blocking (+{dt} DT vs melee) — click to lower

Targeted.title: Targeted Attack
Targeted.hint: Targeted attacks cost extra AP by limb (melee weapons reduce the extra cost by 2, minimum 1). If the damage reaches hit points, a d4 decides the inflicted condition. A critical hit inflicts the severe injury instead (or up to two of the conditions).
Targeted.conditionFlavor: {limb} condition if damage reaches HP: {condition} (attacker may re-roll this d4 up to {rerolls} times)
Targeted.severeInjury: Severe injury ({limb}): {injury} — or choose up to two of the limb's conditions instead.

eyes.label: Eyes
eyes.effect: Total damage is halved; a ranged attack's to-hit modifier is halved
eyes.c1: −5 to all attack rolls for two turns
eyes.c2: Disadvantage on all attack rolls for two turns
eyes.c4: Temporary Blindness — blinded for the next hour or until all hit points are healed
eyes.severe: Eye Gouged — Perception reduced by 2; both eyes gouged = permanently blinded

head.label: Head
head.effect: Damage dice increased by 1 (e.g. 1d10 → 2d10); a ranged attack's to-hit modifier is halved
head.c1: −2 to all attack rolls for two turns
head.c2: −5 to all attack rolls for two turns

arm.label: Arm
arm.effect: Damage dice decreased by 1, to a minimum of 1 (e.g. 2d10 → 1d10)
arm.c1: Target drops whatever they are holding in that arm
arm.c2: −2 to all attack rolls for two turns
arm.c3: −5 to all attack rolls for two turns
arm.c4: Broken Arm — disadvantage on two-armed STR/AGI rolls until treated with a doctor's bag

torso.label: Torso
torso.c4: Gut Wallop — dazed for the next 2 turns

groin.label: Groin
groin.c4: Painful Collapse — falls prone and dazed until the end of their next turn
groin.severe: Intense Agony — goes into shock and is dazed for 2 turns

leg.label: Leg
leg.effect: Damage dice decreased by 1, to a minimum of 1
leg.c1: Can only move a maximum of 30 feet for two turns
leg.c2: Can only move a maximum of 20 feet for two turns
leg.c3: Can only move a maximum of 15 feet for two turns
leg.c4: Leg Cripple — maximum 20 feet of movement per turn until all hit points are healed

object.label: Held or Carried Object
object.effect: The object gains one level of decay; the creature takes no damage
object.c1: The object gains two levels of decay
object.c2: The object flies one foot away
object.severe: The object is destroyed beyond repair (GM's discretion)

fusionCore.label: Fusion Core (Power Armor)
fusionCore.effect: Needs line of sight to the wearer's back. Deals no damage to the armor or its operator and applies no condition; the rolled damage accumulates against the core, overheating the suit every 30

jetEngine.label: Jet Engine
jetEngine.severed: The jet engine is severed — the Handy falls prone and cannot move until it is reattached

Targeted.cannotSever: This limb cannot be severed — apply up to two of the limb's conditions instead.
Targeted.bodyPlan: Only the limbs this body has are listed (pg 9-10).
Targeted.applyBlank: That face of the table prints no condition ({name} is unaffected).
Targeted.applyManual: This condition is resolved at the table — nothing on the sheet expresses it.
Targeted.objectPrompt: The shot was aimed at something {name} is carrying. Pick the object it hit.
Targeted.objectNothingCarried: {name} is carrying nothing that can be hit.
Targeted.objectNoChoice: No condition was chosen, so nothing was applied.
Targeted.objectAlreadyWrecked: {item} is already as decayed as it can get.
Targeted.objectNotHeld: {item} is carried rather than wielded, so nothing was unequipped.
Targeted.clearedByHeal: Healed to full hit points — {count} limb condition(s) cleared (pg 129).
Targeted.applyVetoed: The condition could not be written to {name} — the effect was refused. Nothing was applied and nothing was announced.

Settings.pipboyCustomColorHint: Hex color (e.g. #6ee86e), used when Pip-Boy Color is set to Custom.
Settings.artOverridePathHint: Folder in your Foundry user data holding your own token/item art. Files named after the creature or item (e.g. deathclaw.webp) replace the shipped artwork. Optional tokens/ and icons/ subfolders are searched too.
Settings.artOverrideApplyHint: Re-scan the folder and update artwork on actors and items already in this world.
Settings.artOverrideMissing: Local artwork folder "{path}" not found — shipped artwork is being used.
Settings.artOverrideApplied: Local artwork applied to {actors} actor(s) and {items} item(s).

Damage.noTargets: No targets selected — target tokens first (T)
Damage.applied: {name}: {total} damage — {sp} to Stamina, {hp} to Hit Points ({dt} stopped by DT)
Damage.dying: They drop to 0 HP and are DYING.
Damage.severeInjury: Overflow damage ≥ max HP: they suffer a SEVERE INJURY.
Damage.dpAbsorbed: Power Armor absorbed {dp} with its Defense Points.
Damage.dpDepleted: Power Armor absorbed {dp} and its Defense Points ran out — the pool refills and the suit gains a level of decay.
Damage.dyingHit: Damaged while dying — a failed death save (now {failures}).
Damage.corroded: Corrosive: their armor gains a level of decay (now {decay}).
Damage.corrodedBroken: Corrosive: their armor reaches {decay} levels of decay and is broken.

DeathSave.pickAbility: Add your Luck or Endurance modifier (pg 133) — the value shown is what it is actually worth
DeathSave.penaltyHint: Your leveled conditions cost −{penalty} on a d20, and Luck rolls are exempt from them (pg 124, 132-134). That is why the two numbers above can disagree with the raw modifiers on your sheet. Hold Alt on the button to skip this dialog and take the better of the two.

Aid.snack: Snack — two of these are needed to remove a level of hunger (pg 82), so none was removed automatically.
Aid.inorganic: No stamina restored: this race gains no effects from food, drinks, or chems (pg 8-9).
Aid.blandAsTasty: Ice Cream and Apple Pie: Bland counts as Tasty (pg 52).
Aid.tainted: Tainted: you may flip a Karma Cap to ignore contracting a disease instead (pg 83).
Aid.taintedImmune: Ice Cream and Apple Pie: no disease from Tainted food or drink (pg 52).
Aid.healOverTime: Healing Powder takes hold: {hp} hit points at the start of each of the next {rounds} turns.
Aid.healOverTimeImmune: Healing Powder does nothing for ghouls, robots or gen-2 synths (pg 86).
Aid.healOverTimeTick: Healing Powder restores {hp} hit points ({rounds} turns remaining).

Sheet.tempHpHint: Temporary hit points — spent before hit points and never healed back (Anabolic chems, several perks).
Sheet.wielded: Wielded — in hand. Blocking (pg 127) needs a melee weapon here.
Sheet.defenseHint: Comma-separated damage types (e.g. fire, poison). Resistance halves, vulnerability doubles.
Sheet.levelHelper: Perk points earned: {perks} · Skill points spent {spent} of {skills} (+6 background)
Sheet.karmaCapHint: Karma Caps — click to flip (advantage or re-roll); the GM can flip one back against you.
Sheet.rollHint: Click to roll. Shift-click: advantage. Ctrl-click: disadvantage. Alt-click: sneak attack (hold Alt on the damage roll too).
Sheet.radLocked: Radiation-locked damage — unhealable until all Rads clear
Sheet.apRecycled: Recycled AP carried into the next turn

Radiation.deathByDamage: Radiation damage brought them to 0 hit points — they die. Roll Luck vs DC {dc} to return as a ghoul.
Radiation.deathByLevels: Tenth level of Radiation — they die. Roll Luck vs DC {dc} to return as a ghoul.
Radiation.checkPassed: Radiation check vs DC {dc} — resisted; the DC rises by 2 until all Rads clear
Radiation.immune: This character is not subject to radiation.
Radiation.ghoul: Returns as a ghoul with 1 hit point
Radiation.feral: Returns FERAL — the GM controls this character
Radiation.stayDead: The check fails; they remain dead
Radiation.cleared: Removes {levels} level(s) of Radiation — all Rads gone; radiation-locked damage can now be healed.
Radiation.healingBlocked: No hit points restored: the remaining damage is radiation-locked until all Rads are gone (pg 124).
Radiation.zone: Irradiated zone level {level}: {rolls} checks over {minutes} minutes.
Radiation.zoneCapped: Irradiated zone level {level}: capped at {rolls} checks for {minutes} minutes — roll more by hand if the scene demands it.
Radiation.staminaBlocked: Stamina restored only up to the radiation lock: the rest stays locked until all Rads are gone (pg 124).

Improvised.title: Improvised Attack
Improvised.pick: Load of the object being used
Improvised.hint: Damage, AP cost and thrown range all scale with the object's Load (pg 128). The attack uses your Melee Weapons bonus.
Improvised.loadGap: (the book prints no row for Load 41-49; the 31-40 row is used)

Frightened.escaped: Succeeded by 10 or more — not frightened
Frightened.halfDuration: Succeeded — frightened for half the allotted time (choose Flight, Fight, Freeze, or Fawn)
Frightened.fullDuration: Failed — frightened for the full allotted time (choose Flight, Fight, Freeze, or Fawn)
Frightened.flightOrFreeze: Failed by 5 or more — frightened, and the mode must be Flight or Freeze
Frightened.criticalFailure: Critical failure — frightened for DOUBLE the allotted time, Flight or Freeze only

ActionPoints.overdrawn: Spends {cost} AP with only {spent} in the pool — {over} over budget.
ActionPoints.untracked: Costs {cost} AP (out of combat, so nothing is tracked).

Combat.bleeding: Bleeding ({levels}): takes {damage} hit points at the start of the turn.
Combat.bleedingDeathSave: Bleeding while dying — an automatic failed death save ({failures}).
Combat.notEnoughAP: Not enough Action Points: needs {cost}, has {ap}.
Combat.burning: Burning: {damage} fire damage ({hp} to hit points). {ap} AP to put yourself out (pg 133).
Combat.shortCircuit: Short Circuit ×{levels} (pg 135): {formula} electricity to hit points — {damage} taken.
Combat.shortCircuitDying: Reduced to 0 hit points, so all levels of Short Circuit are removed (pg 135).

Diseases.floorHint: A disease pins {floor} levels here until it is cured.
Diseases.floorBlocked: A disease is holding those levels in place.
Diseases.sleptNothing: Nothing changed — no disease ends on sleep.

Diseases.tooSoon: Too soon — {disease} needs another {hours} h between doses.

Diseases.moveCap: Movement capped at {feet} ft per turn.

bloodWorms.name: Blood worms
bloodWorms.effect: Whenever you take damage to your hit points, you take an additional 1d4 poison damage.

boneWorms.name: Bone worms
boneWorms.effect: Whenever you take damage to your hit points, you gain a random limb condition.

buzzBrain.name: Buzz brain
buzzBrain.effect: Disadvantage on Intelligence ability and skill checks.
buzzBrain.cure: Any food or chem with the Stimulant property.

dysentery.name: Dysentery
dysentery.effect: Four levels of Dehydration that cannot be removed until the disease is gone.
dysentery.cure: Two antibiotics, taken a day apart.

fever.name: Fever
fever.effect: Maximum action points reduced by 3 (minimum 6), and disadvantage on all d20 rolls.
fever.cure: Med-X suppresses it for 1d4 hours; only time cures it.

flapLimb.name: Flap limb
flapLimb.effect: Disadvantage on checks, skill checks, and attack rolls using Strength.

glowingPustules.name: Glowing pustules

heatFlashes.name: Heat flashes

heatFlashes.cure: Sleep, so long as you have no levels of Dehydration.

jellyFingers.name: Jelly fingers
jellyFingers.effect: Attacking with a ranged weapon costs 1 extra action point.

lockJoint.name: Lock joint
lockJoint.effect: Attacking with a melee weapon costs 1 extra action point.

parasites.name: Parasites

radWorms.name: Rad worms
radWorms.effect: You gain a level of Rads every time you sleep.
radWorms.cure: Two RadAway, taken a day apart.

rattleHands.name: Rattle hands
rattleHands.effect: Ranged weapon damage is reduced by 2, to a minimum of 1.

sludgeLung.name: Sludge lung

snotEar.name: Snot ear

swampGas.name: Swamp gas
swampGas.effect: Disadvantage on Charisma ability and skill checks.

swampItch.name: Swamp itch
swampItch.effect: Disadvantage on checks, skill checks, and attack rolls using Agility.

Hazards.hint: Rad Resist checks ignore a gas mask; Toxic Air does not (pg 123).
Hazards.frigid: {minutes} minutes past the {tolerated} you could stand: Hypothermia rises to {levels}.

Environment.insulatedHint: Cold: gains are softened. Heat: gains are doubled. The book means both.

Environment.shelteredHint: Rain and Dust Storm cannot reach you.

Environment.gasMaskHint: Toxic Air's DC drops by 10 and disease is blocked. Never helps in water.

PowerArmor.ceased: The reserve is gone. The suit opens its back, lets its user out, and ceases function (pg 58).
PowerArmor.overrideOffer: The user may instead override the ejection to stay inside — but is then grappled and restrained, and cannot escape unless their Strength score is {strength}. The printed cap on a score is 10, and the suit sets it to 12, so as written there is no way out. Escaping decays the suit by 10 levels.
PowerArmor.overheatEject: With {minutes} minutes or less of allotted time left, an overheating suit ejects its user and ceases function (pg 58).
PowerArmor.coolingOverride: The user may override the automatic cooling to keep the allotted time — but the fusion core then explodes at the end of their next turn: {damage} explosive damage within {short} ft, half within {long} ft, the suit destroyed, its user incinerated, and a Level {level} Irradiated Zone left behind.
PowerArmor.coreHit: The fusion core of {suit} takes {damage} damage ({total} total). It overheats every {threshold}. (The book says the attack deals no damage yet counts damage to the core; this counts rolled damage cumulatively.)

cause.actionPoints: more than its AP threshold spent in one turn
cause.stillOverheated: still overheated at the start of the turn

PowerArmor.noSuit: You are not wearing Power Armor.
PowerArmor.swapHint: Slot a fresh Fusion Core (5 AP). Restores the suit's full allotted time and restarts it if it had ceased function.
PowerArmor.allottedHint: Minutes of operation left. The book prints a total per suit model but never a base drain rate, so only the drains it names — cooling, Tesla Coils, Jet Pack, Explosive vent — are charged automatically.
PowerArmor.decayHint: Decay costs a suit nothing except radiation protection and, at ten levels, the Defense Point refill. Power Armor never breaks (pg 57).
PowerArmor.thresholdHint: AP that may be spent in one turn before the suit overheats (pg 58). Core Assembly raises it to 18 or 20.
PowerArmor.radiationHint: Under six levels of decay the wearer is immune to Radiation; six to nine grants advantage on Rad Resist checks; at ten the suit offers nothing (pg 57).
PowerArmor.coreDamageHint: Damage accumulated from Fusion Core targeted attacks. Every 30 overheats the suit (pg 58).

entry.robot: A Robot cannot use Power Armor at all (pg 9).
entry.needsFitting: A Super Mutant cannot use Power Armor unless it is modded to their body type (pg 11) — this suit needs the Super Mutant Fitting upgrade (pg 59).
entry.fittedOut: This suit carries the Super Mutant Fitting: humans and ghouls can no longer use it (pg 59). Removing the fitting costs the same price or crafting materials again.

PowerArmor.suitTraits: Hydraulic Machine and Longer Strides: Strength counts as 12, size is {size}, and a sprint carries {sprint} feet instead of 50 (+{strides}). Size {size} is reported, not enforced — nothing in this system tracks a creature's size.
PowerArmor.noUpgrade: This suit does not have {upgrade} at the rank that ability requires (pg 59).
PowerArmor.ceasedControl: The suit has ceased function — slot a fresh Fusion Core before using its upgrades.
PowerArmor.upgradesHint: The pg 59 Power Armor upgrades, by rank. Ranks are cumulative and each costs the base price again (pg 58); attaching or removing one takes 15 minutes, not the 1 minute a regular armor upgrade takes.
PowerArmor.syncUpgradesHint: Rebuild the Active Effects a suit's upgrades grant. Run it after editing a rank by hand.
PowerArmor.spendTimeHint: Charge the suit minutes of operation. The book prints a total per suit model and never a base drain rate, so time only passes when someone says it does.
PowerArmor.teslaOn: Switches the Tesla Coils on ({ap} AP). Each creature within {radius} feet takes {damage} electricity damage now and at the start of their turns; the coils burn {minutes} minutes of allotted time each round they stay on (pg 59).
PowerArmor.teslaOff: Switches the Tesla Coils off ({ap} AP).
PowerArmor.teslaDamage: Tesla Coils — every creature within {radius} feet. The book also charges this at the start of each of *their* turns, which this system does not iterate; re-roll it then.
PowerArmor.jetPackFlight: Flies {feet} feet on the Jet Pack ({ap} AP). The book charges 1 minute of allotted time per 10 feet flown "or every second that you fly" — two different rates; distance is what is charged here, rounded up.
PowerArmor.ventFired: Vents explosively on landing — the upgrade requires a fall of at least {fall} feet, which nothing here can measure. Each creature within {radius} feet takes {damage} fire damage and {damage} explosive damage, and the suit loses {minutes} minutes of allotted time (pg 59).
PowerArmor.ventDamage: Explosive vent — every creature within {radius} feet.
PowerArmor.overclockSelf: Deliberately overheats the fusion core ({ap} AP, Overclock Hydraulics rank 2, pg 59).
PowerArmor.overclockActive: Overclock Hydraulics: while overheated you can also move {feet} feet for {ap} AP and your unarmed attacks deal an additional {damage} fire damage (pg 59). Both are reported — this system has no movement budget and no unarmed damage rider.
PowerArmor.bracers: A powerful unarmed attack with Optimized bracers ({ap} AP, {damage} bludgeoning, pg 59). Roll the attack as an ordinary unarmed attack.
PowerArmor.bracersPush: At rank 3 it also pushes the target 15 feet back.
PowerArmor.kineticDynamo: Kinetic dynamo returns {ap} AP for the {decay} level(s) of decay the suit took since the last turn (pg 59).

manual.explosiveShielding: Reduces explosive damage taken by 5 / 10 / 15. Applied when damage is dealt, if the damage pipeline is wired to the suit's shielding.
manual.prismShielding: Reduces laser and plasma damage taken by 5 / 10 / 20. The printed ranks read 5 / 5 / 10; taken as totals, rank 2 would buy nothing, so they are read cumulatively.
manual.reactivePlates: A melee attacker takes a quarter of the damage they dealt, rounded down, twice over at rank 2; at rank 3 they are knocked 15 feet. Reported — this system applies damage to the target the GM has selected, and the attacker is not it.
manual.vatsMatrix: Every targeted attack's additional AP cost drops by 1 per rank, to a floor of 0. The Fusion Core's +5 becomes +3 at rank 2.
manual.targetingHud: 3 AP marks a creature (one, or three at rank 2); damage you deal to a marked creature adds a die, two dice at rank 3. Not automated: a mark is state about another creature, and the extra die belongs to the attack roll.
manual.headlamp: 1 AP for a 40 foot bright cone and 40 more of dim, +10 feet per rank; at rank 3 it blinds creatures within 5 feet if lit in darkness. Not automated: light is token configuration, which this system has never touched.
manual.rustyKnuckles: An unarmed hit makes the target bleed. Not automated: applying Bleeding needs the attack roll to know it landed and on whom.
manual.emergencyProtocolsMove: Rank 1: while under half your hit points you can spend 1 AP to move 10 feet. Not automated: nothing here meters movement.
manual.superMutantFitting: Fits the suit to a Super Mutant. Humans and ghouls can no longer wear it; entering is gated on both counts. Removal costs the same price or materials again.

PowerArmor.shielded: Shielding absorbs {reduced} before the suit takes the rest (pg 59).
PowerArmor.rankHint: Click a rank to install an upgrade at it; clicking the rank a suit already has steps it back down, which is how a rank returns to 0. Ranks are cumulative — a rank 3 upgrade has the abilities of ranks 1, 2 and 3 (pg 58) — and stop at the maximum the pg 59 table prints. Each rank costs the base price again, and attaching or removing one takes 15 minutes rather than the 1 minute a regular armor upgrade takes (pg 57-58).
PowerArmor.setRank: {upgrade} rank {rank}. Click it again to drop back a rank.

automationHint.code: Automated: this system enforces the rule wherever it applies.
automationHint.control: Button: a control on this panel does it, and the suit's state moves.
automationHint.effect: Effect: an Active Effect on the suit carries the bonus. Press “Apply upgrade effects” after changing a rank anywhere but here.
automationHint.helper: Reported: the arithmetic is here and correct, but the place that has to apply it — the damage pipeline, the targeted-attack table, the attack roll — is not part of this subsystem. The number is announced, not enforced.
automationHint.text: Text only: deliberately not automated. Read the upgrade on pg 59 and apply it by hand.

PowerArmor.automationLegend: The badge on each row says how far this system takes that upgrade: Automated and Effect run by themselves, Button needs a press, Reported gives you the number to apply, Text only does nothing mechanically. Hover a badge for the reason.
PowerArmor.teslaButtonHint: 3 AP to switch the coils on or off (pg 59). While on, every creature within 10 feet takes the coils' electricity damage on activation and at the start of their own turns — the second half is re-rolled by hand, because this system does not iterate other creatures' turns — and the suit burns 10 to 25 minutes of allotted time each round they stay on.
PowerArmor.jetPackButtonHint: 1 AP per 5 feet flown, and 1 minute of allotted time per 10 feet (pg 59). The book charges that minute per 10 feet “or every second that you fly”; those are two different rates, and distance is the one that can be metered, so distance is what is charged, rounded up.
PowerArmor.ventButtonHint: On a landing, every creature within 20 feet (30 at rank 3) takes 3d6 fire and 3d6 explosive damage, and the suit loses 20 minutes of allotted time (pg 59). The two damage types are rolled separately, so resistance to one is not resistance to the other.
PowerArmor.ventFallHint: Explosive vent requires a fall of at least {fall} feet (pg 59). Nothing here knows how far a token dropped, so that precondition is yours to check.
PowerArmor.overclockButtonHint: Overclock Hydraulics rank 2: spend 3 AP to overheat the fusion core deliberately (pg 59), because rank 1 is a large buff while overheated. It costs the suit a full cooling cycle, and on a core down to 30 minutes or less it ejects you and stops the suit — the book carves out no exception for choosing it.
PowerArmor.bracersButtonHint: 6 AP for a powerful unarmed attack: 2d6 bludgeoning, rising a die per rank, and a 15-foot push at rank 3 (pg 59). Roll the attack as an ordinary unarmed attack — this rolls the damage the upgrade changes, and reports the push, because nothing here moves tokens.
PowerArmor.databaseButtonHint: 6 AP to learn a creature you can see's HP total, SP total, AC or DT (pg 59). Line of sight is the GM's call, so this reads whoever you have targeted. The book does not say the reading is private, so it posts to chat like any other card.
PowerArmor.pickOneTarget: Target exactly one creature — the Internal database reads one creature's numbers, and this will not guess which.
PowerArmor.syncDone: Upgrade effects rebuilt: {count} effect(s) created, updated or removed.
PowerArmor.reflected: Reactive Plates throw {damage} damage back at {attacker} (pg 59) — a quarter of the damage dealt per rank, to a maximum of two quarters. The rank 2 gloss calls that “effectively half of the total”, which is not what two roundings-down produce on an odd number; the arithmetic is printed twice and the gloss once, so the arithmetic wins.
PowerArmor.reflectedNothing: Reactive Plates catch the blow but the hit was too small to reflect: a quarter of it, rounded down, is nothing (pg 59).
PowerArmor.reflectedKnockback: {attacker} is knocked back {feet} feet (Reactive Plates rank 3, pg 59). Nothing here moves tokens — move them.
PowerArmor.vatsReduced: VATS matrix overlay: additional AP reduced from {printed} to {ap} (pg 59). The suit takes 1 off per rank, to a maximum of rank 2. Pg 130 floors the melee discount at 1 additional AP; pg 59 prints no floor of its own, so a rank 2 suit can take that last point off.
PowerArmor.vatsHint: Costs shown already include your VATS matrix overlay, which is taking up to {ap} AP off the additional cost (pg 59).

Grapple.hint: 3 AP. An Unarmed skill check against 10 + the target's Unarmed skill; success — or a raw 20 — leaves them grappled, which stops them spending AP to move. Nothing but an Escape ends it.
Grapple.natural20: (a raw 20 carries it regardless of the DC)
Grapple.noTarget: Target a creature to grapple first.

Escape.hint: 5 AP. An Unarmed skill check against 10 + the grappler's Unarmed skill; success — or a raw 20 — frees you from a grapple, restraint, or chokehold.
Escape.noDC: Nothing recorded who is holding you, so there is no Unarmed skill to price the DC from — a restraint or a trap needs a DC from the GM (pg 80's bear trap prints its own).
Escape.cleared: Freed from: {statuses} (pg 126 — “a grapple, restrain, or chokehold”). Chokehold is named in that sentence and defined nowhere else in the book, so there is no third condition to clear.
Escape.nothingHeld: Nothing was holding them — the check succeeded against a DC with no condition behind it. Grappled and Restrained are both off.

Unarmed.hint: 3 AP for one strike, 5 AP for two (new in v2.1). 1d4 + your Strength or Agility modifier, bludgeoning. Bare hands have no printed critical hit chance, so a raw 20 is announced and left to the table.
Unarmed.holeyMoley: (Holey Moley: one extra strike for 1 AP, once per turn)
Unarmed.miss: CRITICAL FAILURE — automatic miss (no weapon to decay)
Unarmed.natural20: raw 20 — bare hands have no printed crit chance; the table decides
Unarmed.unpriced: The book prices one unarmed strike at 3 AP and two at 5 AP, and no other bundle — {strikes} has no printed cost.

Help.hint: 6 AP. v2.1 replaced advantage with a number: the creature you aid adds half your bonus in the related skill, rounded down, to their next check. The attack branch still grants advantage on your ally's first attack before your next turn.
Help.descriptionCheck: +{bonus} to the next check, from {helper}'s Help. Spent by the next roll.
Help.descriptionAttack: Advantage on the first attack roll, from {helper}'s Help. The book's window closes at {helper}'s next turn.
Help.gaveCheck: Helps {ally} ({ap} AP) — +{bonus} to their next check, half their {skill} bonus rounded down.
Help.gaveAttack: Helps {ally} attack ({ap} AP) — advantage on their first attack roll before this creature's next turn.
Help.needsSkill: Help adds half your bonus in the related skill — name the skill you are helping with.

Ready.hint: The readied action's own AP plus 2. If the trigger never fires you may recycle half the total at the start of your next turn — new in v2.1, which previously gave nothing back.
Ready.readied: Readies an action ({ap} AP — the action plus the {surcharge} AP surcharge). Trigger: {trigger}. If it never fires, {recycle} AP come back at the start of the next turn.
Ready.freeze: (Frightened — Freeze, pg 134: readying is the one thing AP may be spent on while the source of fear is in sight.)
Ready.fired: The trigger fires — {trigger}. No AP comes back.
Ready.lapsed: The trigger never came. Of {spent} AP committed, {refund} are recycled into the start of the next turn.
Ready.lapsedDazed: The trigger never came, and {spent} AP are lost: a dazed creature cannot recycle AP (pg 133), and this refund is a recycle.

Cover.note: [{degree} — +{ac} to the target's AC (pg 130); this side of the roll never sees an AC, so apply it when you compare]
Cover.noteExplosive: [{degree} — +{ac} to the target's AC, and resistance to explosive and trap damage from beyond the cover (pg 130); the book never says what resistance does to a number]
Cover.totalBlocks: Total cover (pg 130): the target can't be targeted directly by an attack — only an area of effect can reach it.
Cover.creature: [using a creature as cover (pg 130) — a total of {max} or below hits the covering creature instead]
Cover.creatureHit: — {total} is {max} or below: the damage goes to the covering creature (pg 130), applied by hand
Cover.pickDistance: Distance to the target, in feet (pg 21) — leave blank to skip the range bands
Cover.pickObscured: The target is heavily obscured — darkness, fog, dense foliage (pg 118)
Cover.obscuredHint: A heavily obscured target, or a blinded attacker, makes this a blind attack (pg 128): your Luck modifier replaces the skill bonus and a DC of 5 + the distance replaces the target's AC. It needs a distance. Hiding and invisibility are read off the target's own sheet; darkness has no document, so it is declared here. An Infrared Scope (pg 76) exempts the weapon.
Cover.hint: Cover and distance are declared, not measured: the degrees are a GM call ("at least half of its body", "about three-quarters"), and the attacking token is not something a character sheet knows about.
Cover.takeCover: Take Cover (pg 127): 3 AP turns half or three-quarters cover into full cover; attacking gives it up again.

Range.long: [{distance} ft — past this weapon's {normal} ft normal range{shrunk}: disadvantage (pg 21, pg 66)]
Range.beyond: [{distance} ft — past this weapon's {long} ft long range{shrunk}: pg 66 says only a natural 20 hits; pg 21 says you can't attack at all. The book contradicts itself here; pg 66 is followed]
Range.beyondHit: — a natural 20 beyond long range: it hits (pg 66)
Range.beyondMiss: — beyond long range without a natural 20: the attack misses (pg 66)
Range.shrunk: , already cut by weather or Kickback
Range.limbHalved: [Targeting the eyes or head halves this weapon's range (pg 129) — now {normal}/{long} ft]

Crafting.title: Craft {item}
Crafting.hint: A skill check against 10 + the item's Craft DC (pg 92). Meeting the listed bonus crafts it outright with no roll. Failing costs 1d4 of each material, failing by 8 or more costs 1d6, and succeeding by 8 or more saves 1d4 from one material. Not every table rolls Crafting — food is Survival, medicine is Medicine, energy ammunition is Science.
Crafting.pushLuck: Roll anyway to try to save materials (risks failing)
Crafting.dcLabel: Craft DC bonus from the Blueprint Encyclopedia
Crafting.succeededWell: Crafted {item} ×{quantity}, and beat DC {dc} by 8 or more: one material comes in cheaper.
Crafting.failed: {item} was not crafted — the check missed DC {dc}.
Crafting.failedBadly: {item} was not crafted, and the check missed DC {dc} by 8 or more.
Crafting.automatic: {skill} bonus already meets the listed {bonus} — crafted outright, no roll needed.
Crafting.multiCheck: This row prints two requirements under "{heading}": {checks}. Both must be passed.
Crafting.rider: Also printed in the DC cell: {text}
Crafting.materialsLost: Materials lost: {materials}. The rest are still on the bench.
Crafting.alternatives: The printed cell offers alternatives — only the first is costed above: {text}
Crafting.assisted: {count} creature(s) assisting ({names}) — the time above is already halved once per assistant.
Crafting.assistantFailed: {who} failed their check, which fails the whole craft however well anyone else rolled (pg 92).
Crafting.powerArmor: Power Armor: {days} day(s) of work, one check each, and the materials above are the printed daily cost multiplied by the original {multiplier} days (pg 94).
Crafting.powerArmorRestart: One failed day fails the entire armor build — you must restart from nothing (pg 94).
Crafting.workbench: You still need suitable space and tools — a Workbench, or something jury-rigged at the GM's discretion (pg 92).
Crafting.noBlueprint: {item} carries no Blueprint Encyclopedia entry, so there is no recipe to follow.
Crafting.uncraftable: {item} cannot be crafted: the Encyclopedia prints "{text}".
Crafting.modifier: {item} is a modifier row, not a recipe — its {text} is added to a base item's DC (pg 102), so craft the base item instead.
Crafting.unparsed: {item}'s Craft DC cell reads "{text}", which is more than one number. Supply the DC bonus by hand.
Crafting.drinkGate: Brewing any drink needs Crafting, Survival and Science all at +8 or better (pg 115). Short in: {skills}.

Bench.title: Crafting Bench
Bench.browseHint: Search the Item Blueprint Encyclopedia (pg 94-115) for something to make.
Bench.skillsNote: Fourteen of the Encyclopedia's thirty-three tables head their DC column with a skill other than Crafting — Survival for food, Medicine for medicine, Science for energy ammunition, Explosives for the two explosives tables (pg 94-115). Each recipe below prints the check it would actually be rolled with.
Bench.materialsNote: Materials are listed, never deducted: nothing in this system represents steel, adhesive or a crafting material, so the chat card prints exactly what a build costs and the table settles it (pg 92).
Bench.noRecipes: Nothing on this sheet carries an Encyclopedia recipe. Browse the equipment compendium to pick something to make.
Bench.autoTitle: Your bonus already meets the listed requirement, so the item is simply made — no roll at all (pg 92).
Bench.craftHint: Craft another one of these. Shows the check, the materials and the time before anything is rolled.
Bench.heading: Printed column heading: {heading}
Bench.automaticNote: Automatic success — your bonus meets the listed requirement, so this is simply made with no roll (pg 92).
Bench.rollNote: Your bonus falls short of the listed requirement, so this is a check against 10 + the printed Craft DC (pg 92).
Bench.powerArmorDays: Power Armor: {days} day(s) of work with a check every day, and one failed day loses the entire build (pg 94).
Bench.drinkGate: Brewing any drink needs Crafting, Survival and Science all at +{minimum} or better (pg 115). Short in: {skills}.
Bench.dcOverride: Craft DC bonus override (leave blank to use the printed cell)
Bench.dcHint: Only fill this in for GM fiat. Supplying a bonus replaces the printed cell entirely, so a row that prints two checks would be reduced to one.
Bench.dcNeeded: This row's DC cell is not a single number, so the printed bonus cannot be used as-is — supply the bonus the table should be rolled against.
Bench.assistHint: Each assistant halves the crafting time. An assistant whose own skill falls short of the requirement must roll too, and their failure fails the whole craft however well you roll (pg 92).
Bench.assistNone: Target one or more tokens before opening this dialog to craft with assistance (pg 92). An assistant is not a number: one who falls short of the requirement has to roll, so they need a sheet of their own.
Bench.pickHint: {count} recipes ship with the equipment compendium (pg 94-115). Narrow by table, by name, or both.
Bench.resultHint: {count} recipes match, grouped by the table they are printed in — the table is what decides which skill the check uses. Every DC shown is 10 + the printed Craft DC bonus (pg 92).
Bench.noMatches: No recipe in the Encyclopedia matches that.
Bench.noPack: The equipment compendium is not available, so there are no recipes to browse.

FirstAid.bleedingHint: A DC 15 Medicine check on a creature within 5 feet, costing 6 AP and 1 cloth junk item, ends every level of Bleeding (pg 21, 23). The cloth is taken from a “Junk: Cloth” stack on this sheet if there is one, before the roll; if there is not, the check still happens and the card says the cloth was missing. Deduct the AP by hand. A First Aid Kit or Doctor's Bag Tourniquet removes only two levels for the same 6 AP, but needs no check and no cloth.
FirstAid.bleedingCheck: First aid on {target} — Medicine vs DC {dc} to end Bleeding
FirstAid.bleedingSucceeded: Stops the bleeding on {target} — {levels} level(s) of Bleeding ended.
FirstAid.bleedingFailed: The bleeding on {target} does not stop — the Medicine check missed DC {dc}. Failure carries no further penalty and the attempt can be made again, but the 6 AP and the cloth bought the attempt, not the result: the book's sentence makes only the check conditional.
FirstAid.floorBlocked: {target}'s remaining {levels} level(s) of Bleeding are held in place by a disease (pg 120) — first aid cannot reach them.
FirstAid.floorRemains: {levels} level(s) of Bleeding stay: a disease is holding them in place (pg 120).
FirstAid.cost: Costs {ap} AP and {cloth} cloth junk item, within {feet} feet (pg 21, 23). The cloth is spent from the sheet when a “Junk: Cloth” stack is on it; the AP is reported and never deducted, and nothing here measures the 5 feet.
FirstAid.stabilizeHint: 6 AP and a Medicine check against 10 minus the dying creature's Endurance modifier (pg 131). On a success they return to 1 hit point and their death saves are cleared. Pg 21/23 print a different DC for the same action — 10 plus their failed death saves minus their successful ones; this system follows the combat chapter and shows the other number on the card.
FirstAid.stabilizeCheck: Administering first aid to {target} — Medicine vs DC {dc}
FirstAid.stabilizeFailed: {target} is not stabilised — the Medicine check missed DC {dc}. The attempt can be made again.
FirstAid.stabilizeCost: Costs {ap} AP (pg 131). Spend it by hand. Pg 21/23 add “at GM's discretion” to this attempt.
FirstAid.otherPrinting: The book prints two DCs for this. Pg 21/23 would have asked for {dc} (10 + failed − successful death saves); this system follows pg 131's 10 − Endurance modifier, because the combat chapter beats the ability-score summary.
FirstAid.stabilizeBleeding: {target} has {levels} level(s) of Bleeding. Pg 133 redirects *healing* on a bleeding creature into removing two levels instead of restoring hit points; pg 131 sets stabilising against healing (“if healing is unavailable”), so this system treats them as different acts and hands back the hit point. Overrule it here if your table reads it the other way — and note a bleeding dying creature also fails a death save every turn.
FirstAid.deathSavesCleared: Death saves cleared ({successes} success(es) / {failures} failure(s) discarded). The book does not say they clear; at 1 hit point the creature is no longer dying, and three successful death saves clear them the same way (pg 131).
FirstAid.notDying: {target} is not dying — first aid to stabilise only reaches a creature at 0 hit points (pg 131).
FirstAid.tooLate: {target} has failed all of their death saves ({failures}) — no Medicine check brings them back (pg 21, 23, 131).
FirstAid.title: First Aid
FirstAid.pickOne: Target exactly one creature to treat.
FirstAid.targetHint: Target a creature on the canvas, then press a button. Both actions are a Medicine check and cost 6 AP, reported rather than deducted.
FirstAid.selfDying: You are dying yourself — someone else has to make this check.
FirstAid.notAKit: {item} is not a First Aid Kit or a Doctor's Bag — only those two carry the pg 86 actions.
FirstAid.kitLacksAction: A {item} does not offer {action}. Set Bone is printed in the Doctor's Bag entry only (pg 86).
FirstAid.kitHint: Pg 86. None of these rolls anything — that is what the kit buys over a Medicine check, and what it pays for in supplies. This kit holds {uses} action(s); after the last one “the supplies are used and it no longer functions”. AP and minutes are reported, not deducted, and “so long as they are next to you” is on your honour — nothing here reads token positions.
FirstAid.kitExhausted: {item}: {spent} of {total} action(s) used — the supplies are spent and this one no longer functions (pg 86).

kitHints.tourniquet: 6 AP, remove up to two levels of bleeding
kitHints.painKiller: 6 AP, heal a dying creature 1 hit point
kitHints.stitchWounds: 10 minutes, heal double their healing rate + your Medicine bonus
kitHints.setBone: 10 minutes, remove Broken Arm or Broken Leg (Doctor's Bag only)

FirstAid.tourniquetDone: Tourniquet on {target}: {levels} level(s) of Bleeding removed (up to {max}, pg 86), {remaining} remaining. The DC 15 Medicine check on pg 21/23 removes every level for the same 6 AP, but needs a check and a cloth junk item.
FirstAid.painKillerDone: Pain Killer: {target} returns to {hp} hit point (pg 86). No check — this is the no-roll alternative to the pg 131 Medicine check.
FirstAid.painKillerRedirected: Pg 86 calls this healing, and pg 133 refuses hit points to a healed bleeding creature — so {target} sheds Bleeding and stays at 0, still dying. This system rules the redirect off for the pg 131 stabilise action, because pg 131 sets stabilising against healing in its own first sentence (“if healing is unavailable”); pg 86 draws no such contrast and uses the word “heal”, so it stands here. Administer First Aid (Medicine, DC 10 − their Endurance modifier) is the route that gets them up. Overrule this at the table if you read it otherwise — this is the most arguable call in the chapter.
FirstAid.stitchDone: Stitch Wounds: {target} heals {hp} hit point(s) — double their healing rate ({rate}) plus your Medicine bonus ({medicine}), pg 86.
FirstAid.stitchNothing: {target} has nothing for Stitch Wounds to heal, so the kit keeps its use. The book never says whether supplies are spent on an action with no effect; an 80-cap item destroyed by a misclick is the worse guess.
FirstAid.setBoneDone: Set Bone on {target}: {minutes} minutes (pg 86). No Broken Arm to remove. Broken Leg appears on pg 86 and nowhere else in the book — the pg 129 leg row’s fourth condition is Leg Cripple, which a full heal removes instead. The use is spent because the book spends it.
FirstAid.efficientDiagnosis: Efficient Diagnosis ×{ranks}: +{hp} hit points (pg 38). The perk's alternative — flip a Karma Cap to heal double instead — is yours to take; no cap-spend workflow exists here to do it for you. “On another creature” is literal, so treating yourself gains nothing.
FirstAid.setBoneTreated: {target} is treated over {minutes} minutes — {count} Broken Arm condition(s) removed (pg 86). "Broken Leg" is named on pg 86 and defined nowhere in the book; the leg row prints Leg Cripple, which a full heal removes.

CombatPanel.title: Combat Actions
CombatPanel.grappleTargetHint: Grapple targets the creature you have targeted, and refuses unless that is exactly one (pg 126). Escape takes no target — it rolls against whoever is holding you. Shift-click for advantage, Ctrl-click for disadvantage.
CombatPanel.grappledState: Grappled (pg 134): you cannot spend AP to move. Nothing but an Escape ends it — the book names no other trigger, so nothing here watches for one.
CombatPanel.restrainedState: Restrained (pg 135): you cannot move, and damage you take cannot be subtracted from your stamina points. Escape ends a restraint too (pg 126).
CombatPanel.heldWithoutRecord: Something is holding you that no Grapple recorded — a restraint, a trap, or a Clasp weapon (pg 61, 80, 81). Escape will ask for a DC, because pg 126 prices it off a creature's Unarmed skill and none of those is a creature.
CombatPanel.notHeld: Nothing is holding you: no Grapple recorded a grappler, and neither the grappled nor the restrained status is set. Escape frees you from "a grapple, restrain, or chokehold" (pg 126) and there is none to roll against.
CombatPanel.escapeDcHint: pg 126 sets the DC at 10 + the creature's Unarmed skill, and a trap or a rope has none. The book answers that with a bespoke DC per object — pg 80's bear trap prints "a Strength ability check equal to 15" to pry it open — so the GM names one here. Clasp (pg 61) still describes this roll in v2.0's vocabulary; read as disadvantage on the pg 126 check, which is the only reading that leaves the property doing anything.
CombatPanel.helpNoTarget: Target the ally you are helping first (pg 127).
CombatPanel.helpPick: Related skill — your bonus, and the half your ally receives
CombatPanel.helpHint: v2.1 replaced advantage with a number: the creature you aid adds half your bonus in the related skill, rounded down, to their next check (pg 127). The book prints no floor, so a negative bonus hands your ally a penalty. The attack branch takes no skill and is the half v2.1 did not change — advantage on your ally's first attack roll before your next turn.
CombatPanel.helpTargetHint: Help targets the creature you have targeted, and refuses unless that is exactly one. 6 AP either way (pg 126).
CombatPanel.helpHeldCheck: +{bonus} on your next roll. Spent by the next roll you make, and by nothing else — the book says "their next ability check", which is a trigger and not a clock.
CombatPanel.helpHeldAttack: Advantage on your first attack roll. The book's window closes at the helper's next turn (pg 127), which is a deadline about somebody else's turn — honour it at the table.
CombatPanel.readyCost: The readied action's own AP (a further {surcharge} AP is added)
CombatPanel.readyNeedsTrigger: Ready needs a trigger and an AP cost: pg 126 says "you must specify what the trigger is and spend the necessary AP with an additional 2 AP".
CombatPanel.fireHint: The trigger occurred, so the action happens and no AP comes back (pg 126).
CombatPanel.lapseHint: The trigger never came: clear this readied action and bank {refund} AP into your recycle pool (pg 126). Lapsing several together can pay more, because the halving floors once rather than per row.
CombatPanel.readyRefund: If none of this fires, {refund} AP recycle at the start of your next turn (pg 126).
CombatPanel.readyRefundDazed: Nothing recycles: a dazed creature cannot recycle AP (pg 133), and Ready's refund is a recycle (pg 126). Neither rule cites the other; this is the reading that leaves both meaning something.
CombatPanel.readyMultiple: More than one action is readied, and Ready resolves per creature rather than per marker — either control here clears every one of them and settles the refund on the total.
CombatPanel.frightenedState: Frightened (pg 134). Flight, Fight, Freeze or Fawn is your choice and nothing here gates it.

Bleeding.healRedirect: No hit points restored: “If a creature who has any levels of bleeding is healed, they do not gain any hit points, instead they remove two levels of bleeding” (pg 133). {refused} hit point(s) of healing became {shed} level(s) of Bleeding shed — {levels} level(s) remain.
Bleeding.healRedirectFloor: No hit points restored, and no Bleeding shed either: pg 133 refuses the {refused} hit point(s) because the creature is bleeding, and a disease is holding all {levels} remaining level(s) in place (pg 120). The book states both rules and never says what happens when they meet; the hit points are refused because pg 133's trigger is simply having levels of Bleeding.

Progression.title: Levelling, Magazines & Caps
Progression.gmOnly: Only the GM can award XP — it writes to every player character in the world.
Progression.noParty: No player-owned characters to award XP to.
Progression.awardHint: Hand out an XP award to the whole party (pg 5), with the four printed modifiers and the catch-up rule.
Progression.awardDialogHint: The book prints no table of award amounts anywhere in 136 pages — the base is the GM's own number, and everything below modifies it. Percentages are taken of the base and summed, then rounded down; the death award is flat and is added afterwards. Every player character then rises to the party's highest total (pg 5).
Progression.awardDowned: Player characters who fell to 0 hit points (+10% each)
Progression.awardCreature: Creature Discovery — first combat sequence with this creature (+20%)
Progression.awardLocation: Location Discovery — first rest in this place (+20%)
Progression.awardDeaths: Player characters permanently dead (+1000 XP each, flat)
Progression.awardBreakdown: Base {base} · 0 HP +{downed} · Creature +{creature} · Location +{location} · Death +{death} (modifiers totalled {percent}%, rounded down; pg 5)
Progression.awardLineCatchUp: {name}: +{xp} XP, +{caught} catching up to the party (pg 5) → {total}
Progression.awardLevelUp: Owed a level: {names}. Levelling is a set of choices (pg 5), so take it from the sheet when you are ready.
Progression.applyLevelHint: Set this character's level to the one their XP total entitles them to (1000 XP per level, pg 5). Only ever raises it — the book has no rule for losing a level.
Progression.levelled: Levels up: {from} → {level}. Spend the perk point — and any skill points — from this panel (pg 5).
Progression.levelledHint: Hit points and stamina follow the level automatically (pg 5-6, Level Up Table).
Progression.noLevelWaiting: No level is waiting: this character's XP does not yet reach the next one (pg 5).
Progression.levelMismatch: Level {level} on the sheet, but {suggested} XP-earned (1000 XP per level, pg 5).
Progression.spendSkillHint: Each point spent in a skill grants it a permanent +1 (pg 5). {left} unspent by this ledger. Skill points arrive at 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, 21st, 25th and 29th level, 3/4/5 at a time depending on Intelligence (pg 5-6).
Progression.spentSkill: Spends {points} skill point(s) on {skill} — a permanent +{points} (pg 5). {left} left.
Progression.notEnoughSkillPoints: That would spend {wanted} skill points and only {left} are unspent (pg 5). Raise the level first, or edit the skill directly if the points came from somewhere the ledger never saw.
Progression.spendPerkHint: A perk point raises one ability score by 1 or takes a perk you meet the requirements for (pg 5) — the same one point either way. {left} unspent. You gain one at every level except 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th and 19th (pg 5).
Progression.perkDocumentHint: Taking a perk records the choice against the point; drag the perk itself from the compendium as usual. Requirements are printed in prose on all 186 perks and are not checked here.
Progression.spentPerk: Spends a perk point on {perk} (pg 5). Add the perk item itself from the compendium.
Progression.noPerkPoints: No perk points left — this level grants {total} in total (pg 5).
Progression.abilityCapped: {ability} is already {score}, the printed maximum for a player character (pg 20).
Progression.noSpends: Nothing recorded yet. The budgets above are what the level grants; this ledger is what became of them.
Progression.undoHint: Hand the point back and reverse what it bought. A perk row only clears the receipt — the perk item is yours to delete.
Progression.undoAbility: Hands back a perk point; {ability} returns to {to}.
Progression.undoPerk: Hands back the perk point recorded against {perk}. The perk item, if there is one, is untouched.
Progression.undoBelowZero: Cannot undo: the ledger claims {points} point(s) in {skill} but the skill only shows {current}. The two have drifted — fix the skill by hand rather than letting this hide it.
Progression.unledgered: {points} skill point(s) on the sheet that this ledger never issued — ordinary for a background character (three +2s, pg 13-18). A negative figure means the ledger and the skills disagree.
Progression.noMagazines: No skill magazines read or carried. Each grants +1 to its skill until you rest, and a permanent +1 once five different issues of the same title are read (pg 88).
Progression.readHint: Read one issue (pg 88). You will be asked which issue number — the book asks the player to track them by hand, and nothing on the item says which one it is.
Progression.issueHint: Pg 88's own example is “¡La Fantoma! issue #4 read”. An issue already on the ledger gives nothing — “Once you read an issue of a skill magazine you can no longer gain its benefits” — but it is still consumed.
Progression.readDialogMinutes: Reading takes {minutes} minute(s) — 5 minus your Intelligence modifier (pg 88).
Progression.readDialogAp: Reading costs {ap} AP, because 5 minus your Intelligence modifier has reached 0 (pg 88).
Progression.readMagazine: Reads {item}, issue #{issue}. {time} Time and AP are reported, not deducted.
Progression.issueAlreadyRead: Issue #{issue} of {item} was already read — no benefit (pg 88). The copy is still used up.
Progression.magazineBonus: +1 {skill} until you rest. {read} of {needed} different issues read.
Progression.magazinePermanent: Five different issues read — {skill} permanently increases by 1 (pg 88). The until-rest +1 from this issue still applies on top of it until the next rest; the book prints them as two separate sentences and never says one replaces the other.
Progression.clearMagazinesHint: Drop every “+1 until you rest” magazine bonus (pg 88). Permanent bonuses stay. Press this after a rest until Rest itself calls it.
Progression.magazineNote: Two issues of the same title before a rest refresh the same +1 rather than stacking — the table prints one +1 per magazine and the book never contemplates two at once. The permanent +1 arrives once, at five different issues; there is no printed second one at ten.
Progression.unknownMagazine: Cannot tell which skill {item} raises — the title is not one of the fourteen printed on pg 88 and its effect text names no skill. Rename it to the printed title, or set its effect text, rather than have it raise the wrong skill.
Progression.unknownMagazineRow: {title} matches none of the fourteen magazines on pg 88, so it grants nothing.
Progression.badIssue: Give a whole issue number of 1 or more.
Progression.discountReady: Discount available: a percentage off one purchase equal to your Barter skill bonus, then unavailable until you rest {hours} hours (pg 22).
Progression.discountUsed: Discount spent — it returns after a {hours}-hour rest (pg 22). Note this system's long rest is 6 hours (pg 119); the Discount prints its own 8.
Progression.buyHintShort: Spend caps on a purchase, optionally applying Barter's Discount (pg 22).
Progression.buyHint: {caps} caps held. Barter's Discount would take {percent}% off (pg 22). The item itself is not created — pg 22 is a rule about paying, and the goods arrive from the GM the usual way.
Progression.buyDiscount: Use Barter's Discount (once per {hours}-hour rest, pg 22)
Progression.buyDiscountSpent: Barter's Discount is already spent — it returns after a {hours}-hour rest (pg 22)
Progression.discountApplied: Barter's Discount: {percent}% off {list} caps, saving {saved} (pg 22). Not available again until an {hours}-hour rest.
Progression.discountNothing: The Discount saved nothing at this price — a Barter bonus of {bonus} rounds down to 0 caps here. The book gives no rounding rule; this system rounds the discount down, as it does everywhere else the book is silent.
Progression.notEnoughCaps: That costs {price} caps and only {caps} are held. The book never lets a character go into debt.
Progression.discountSpent: Barter's Discount is already spent — it returns after a {hours}-hour rest (pg 22).
Progression.resetDiscountHint: Hand Barter's Discount back without an 8-hour rest — a GM override for a rest the sheet never saw (pg 22).

Movement.title: Movement
Movement.noBudget: Prices, not a budget — nothing here counts feet moved (pg 116-118)
Movement.climbHint: 3 AP per 5 feet on a scalable surface, 4 on a sheer or treacherous one, and 1 less with climbing gear — except on treacherous surfaces, where gear is required and takes nothing off (pg 116-117). The AP is reported, never deducted.
Movement.rate: {ap} AP per 5 ft ({geared} AP with climbing gear)
Movement.gearOnly: {ap} AP per 5 ft, and impossible without climbing gear
Movement.climbImpossible: A {surface} surface cannot be climbed without climbing equipment of some kind (pg 117). No AP is priced, because the book forbids the climb rather than pricing it.
Movement.climbCard: Climbing {feet} ft up a {surface} surface {gear}: {ap} AP, at {rate} AP per 5 ft (pg 116-117).
Movement.climbLimit: You can keep climbing for {rounds} round(s) — your Endurance score of {endurance}, minimum one. At the start of your next turn after climbing past that limit, you fall (pg 116). Nothing here counts your climbing turns; when you pass the limit, press Fall.
Movement.offBalance: The book says you are “off-balance (see pg #)” while climbing or swimming. The cross-reference is unfilled and “off-balance” is defined on no page of the book, so nothing mechanical is applied for it.
Movement.offBalanceHint: Climbing and swimming both make you “off-balance (see pg #)” — an unfilled reference to a rule the book never prints. Nothing is applied for it.
Movement.swimHint: 2 AP per 5 feet in still or rushing water, 3 in treacherous, and 1 more while underwater (pg 117). Rushing and treacherous waters also drag you at the start of your turn whether you spend AP or not.
Movement.currentNote: pushes you {feet} ft at the start of your turn
Movement.swimCard: Swimming {feet} ft across {water}: {ap} AP, at {rate} AP per 5 ft (pg 117).
Movement.diveCard: Swimming {feet} ft underwater through {water}: {ap} AP, at {rate} AP per 5 ft — the printed rate plus 1 AP per 5 ft for being under (pg 117).
Movement.currentPush: {water} push you {feet} ft in a direction of the GM's choosing at the start of your turn, whether or not you spend any AP (pg 117).
Movement.swimLimit: You can keep swimming treacherous water for {rounds} round(s) — your Endurance score of {endurance}, minimum one. At the start of your next turn after that, you begin to drown (pg 117). The limit is printed only for treacherous water; still and rushing water have none.
Movement.breathReminder: Underwater you can hold your breath for {seconds} second(s) (pg 117). Use the breathing controls to run the clock.
Movement.jumpHint: A long jump reaches 5 × your Strength modifier (minimum 5 ft) and costs 1 AP per 5 feet cleared; a high jump reaches 3 + your Strength modifier (minimum 1 ft) and costs 1 AP per foot. Both halve if the last two AP you spent were not on moving. Going further costs the AP first and then a Strength check (pg 117).
Movement.jumpRow: {moved} ft for {movedAp} AP after moving · {standing} ft for {standingAp} AP standing
Movement.movedLabel: The last two AP I spent were to move
Movement.jumpMoved: The last two AP spent were on movement, so the full distance is available (pg 117 — they may have been spent last turn, on a readied action, or through the Commander perk).
Movement.jumpStanding: The last two AP spent were not on movement, so the distance is halved (pg 117).
Movement.jumpUnaffordable: That jump costs {ap} AP and only {available} AP is showing. “If you do not have enough AP to clear the jump, you cannot jump on this turn” (pg 117) — reported, not enforced: this system does not spend AP.
Movement.jumpCheck: {kind} — Strength check to clear {extra} extra ft, DC {dc}
Movement.jumpApSpentAnyway: The jump failed and the {ap} AP is spent regardless — “you still use the AP it would have taken to clear the distance” (pg 117).
Movement.sprintHint: 5 AP to move 50 feet in a line (pg 117, pg 127). Stopping or being obstructed ends the movement, and no AP comes back.
Movement.sprintCard: Sprint: {ap} AP to move {feet} ft in a line (pg 117, pg 127).
Movement.sprintDustStorm: A Dust Storm halves a sprint (pg 122), so this run covers half the printed 50 ft.
Movement.sprintTerrain: Difficult terrain does not surcharge a sprint the way it surcharges ordinary movement — it ends it. “If you stop or are obstructed by difficult terrain before you finish this movement, your movement ends” (pg 117), “and you do not regain any action points” (pg 127). Neither printing says whether you finish the five feet you were entering.
Movement.sprintEnds: This sprint ends where the difficult terrain begins, with no AP returned.
Movement.fallHint: Damage, prone, and a limb condition, all by size (pg 117-118). A Medium creature takes 1d6 impact damage per 10 feet to a maximum of 150d6, lands prone, and gains a random arm and leg condition if the damage reaches its hit points.
Movement.fallCapped: Capped at the printed maximum of {dice} dice ({formula}); a longer fall rolls no more (pg 118).
Movement.fallTiny: A tiny creature takes no falling damage “unless they land on something hazardous” (pg 118) — the hazard is the GM's call and is not rolled here.
Movement.fallNoDamage: {feet} ft is short of one whole damage increment, so the fall rolls no dice at all (pg 118).
Movement.fallSoaked: No limb conditions: the damage never reached hit points, and the rule reads “if this damage is dealt to the creature's hit points” (pg 118).
Movement.fallLimbPick: Falling — arm or leg? (tiny creatures gain one condition, not one per limb, pg 118)
Movement.holdHint: 1 + your Endurance modifier in minutes, minimum 30 seconds (pg 117, pg 118). The clock is a marker on your sheet and a person advances it — nothing here is on a timer.
Movement.breathStart: Holding breath: {seconds} second(s) — 1 minute plus an Endurance modifier of {endurance}, minimum 30 seconds (pg 117-118).
Movement.breathPenaltyRule: Every time you take damage, or use more than half your AP on your turn, that total drops by 30 seconds (pg 117).
Movement.breathOut: Out of breath — {rounds} round(s) before dropping.
Movement.breathRemaining: {seconds} second(s) of breath left, after {penalties} penalt(ies) of 30 seconds each (pg 117).
Movement.spendHint: Burn held breath. When it runs out you begin to drown (pg 117-118).
Movement.breathGone: Out of breath. {rounds} round(s) to reach air (your Endurance modifier, minimum one) before dropping to 0 hit points (pg 118).
Movement.breathNone: This creature is not holding its breath.
Movement.breathAlreadyOut: This creature is already out of breath and drowning.
Movement.penaltyHint: Took damage, or used more than half your AP on your turn: your breath drops by 30 seconds, which the book also scores as 6 rounds (pg 117). Neither trigger is detected automatically — damage is not hooked, and AP is not spent through this system at all.
Movement.breathPenaltyTaken: Breath reduced by {seconds} seconds (penalty {penalties}); {remaining} second(s) left (pg 117).
Movement.suffocationRule: “At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again” (pg 118).
Movement.drowning: Drowning — {rounds} round(s) before dropping to 0 hit points (pg 118).
Movement.tickHint: Advance the drowning clock one round (pg 118).
Movement.notSuffocating: This creature is not out of breath.
Movement.suffocationDropped: Out of air: drops to 0 hit points and is dying (pg 118). Stamina points go to 0 with it, as they do for anyone who drops to 0 hit points (pg 131).
Movement.suffocationLock: While it cannot breathe it “can't regain hit points or be stabilized” (pg 118). That lock is reported, not enforced — this system has no healing gate keyed to suffocation, so the first-aid controls will still work on this creature. Honour it at the table.
Movement.breathEnded: Reached air. The breath clock stops; nothing is healed by it.
Movement.airHint: Stop the clock. Nothing is restored — reaching air only lifts the healing lock (pg 118).
Movement.mountLabel: Mount's maximum travel distance in miles (0 = use your own)
Movement.travelHint: 18, 24 or 30 miles a day, and a slow pace scouts while a fast one gets ambushed (pg 116). You may travel 8 + half your Endurance modifier hours; every hour past that is a level of fatigue, and walking at least half your maximum distance on foot is one more.
Movement.travelCard: {mode}, {pace} pace: {hours} hour(s) covering {miles} mi (maximum {max} mi; hour limit {limit}) (pg 116).
Movement.travelSneak: Passive Sneak {sneak} at a {pace} pace — the pace's base plus the party's average Group Sneak bonus. Creatures whose passive sense is lower cannot detect the party unless it blows its own cover (pg 116).
Movement.travelTerrain: {terrain}: the distance travelled is divided accordingly (pg 116). A route that is only partly difficult has no printed resolution, so one tier is applied to the whole leg.
Movement.travelFatigue: {levels} level(s) of fatigue, for a total of {total} — {hours} from hours past the limit, {roads} from The Roads Walked (at least {threshold} mi on foot) (pg 116).
Movement.travelFatigueCapped: {lost} further level(s) went nowhere: fatigue stops at {max} (pg 136).
Movement.travelExempt: {mode}: no levels of fatigue for the journey (pg 116).
Movement.travelPassengerRuling: The book contradicts itself about passengers. Its opening sentence exempts anyone who rides “in a caravan, on the back of a beast, or drive[s] a vehicle”; its closing sentence says the vehicle rule “does not apply to any characters riding in a vehicle that they are not driving”. Ruled for the opening sentence — a passenger is exempt from fatigue, and what the closing sentence denies them is the driver's doubled distance. Overrule it here if your table reads it the other way.
Movement.travelMaxRuling: “Maximum travel distance” is used four times on pg 116 and defined nowhere. Read here as the pace's speed times your own hour limit — mph × (8 + half your Endurance modifier) — which reproduces the printed 18/24/30 mile table exactly at a modifier of 0. An inference, not a printed rule.
Movement.reported: Tracked, not enforced: the AP is spent from the pool, no movement budget is kept, and nothing is ever refused.
Movement.crawlUnpriced: Crawling has no rate and no AP cost anywhere in the book. Prone (pg 135) and Severed Leg/Foot (pg 129) both make crawling a creature's only movement, and no page prices it — so there is no crawl control here, and inventing one would be inventing a rule.

Light.noScene: There is no scene to light — open one first.
Light.brightNote: {level} (pg 118): most creatures see normally. Even gloomy days provide bright light.
Light.dimNote: {level} (pg 118-119): a lightly obscured area — disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on sight, passive sense −5, and every ranged weapon's range halved.
Light.darknessNote: {level} (pg 118-119): a heavily obscured area — vision is blocked entirely and a creature effectively suffers the Blinded condition (pg 133) when trying to see anything in it.
Light.lightNote: Disadvantage on sight-based Perception, passive sense {sense}, ranged range ×{fraction}.
Light.blindedNote: Vision is blocked: effectively Blinded (pg 118 → pg 133) — sight-based ability checks fail automatically, and attacks against you have advantage.
Light.blindsightNote: Blindsight {feet} ft (pg 119): perceived without relying on sight, so nothing here obscures it.
Light.nightvisionNote: Nightvision {feet} ft (pg 119): darkness within that range is only lightly obscured, in shades of gray.
Light.applied: Vision cutoffs applied to {count} token(s) — {level}, {cutoff}. Press Clear to hand the tokens back their own vision.
Light.noTokens: No token on this scene has vision enabled, so there was nothing to cap.
Light.cleared: Vision restored on {count} token(s) exactly as it was authored.
Light.nothingToClear: No token on this scene is carrying a vision override.
Light.flames: Flames (pg 118): {radius} ft across from the origin, dealing {formula} fire damage and Burning, spreading {spread} ft in all directions each round.
Light.flamesDamage: Flames, {radius} ft (pg 118) — {formula} fire damage, and the creature gains Burning
Light.noOneBurning: Nothing is standing in the flames.
Light.extinguished: The flames are put out with {means} (pg 118). The book gives no check, no quantity and no action cost for any of the three means, so nothing was rolled.

Stealth.title: Stealth & Combat Actions
Stealth.targetHint: Hide reads the passive sense of every creature you have targeted and resolves per observer — one roll can hide you from two guards and not from their sergeant (pg 127). Search contests the one creature you target, if they are hiding. Determine Surprise takes the whole opposing side. Shift-click for advantage, Ctrl-click for disadvantage.
Stealth.actionsTitle: The rest of the pg 126 table
Stealth.passiveSneakHint: pg 116: while travelling, creatures whose passive sense is lower than the party's Passive Sneak score cannot detect them — unless the party blows its cover by entering combat, making noise, or becoming obvious, which stays the GM's call. This is the second thing in the book that consumes Group Sneak. Travel distance, the fatigue rule, and each pace's advantage or disadvantage on Combat Sequence belong to the Movement chapter, not to this panel.
Stealth.sneakAttackOn: Sneak attack against {target} (pg 128): your attack is a critical hit and ignores their stamina points, but must still beat their AC. Tick the sneak-attack box on the attack roll.
Stealth.advantageOnly: Hidden from {target}: advantage on your attack roll (pg 24) — but not a sneak attack. pg 127 is explicit that enemies still know your general location, and pg 128 needs them unaware of your presence. Surprise (pg 125) is what supplies that.
Stealth.nothingOn: Nothing stealthy applies against {target} right now: you are not hidden from them and they are not surprised.

Hide.title: Hide
