Hide.hint: 6 AP. A Sneak check against the passive sense of every nearby enemy; you are hidden from each one whose passive sense your roll beats (pg 126-127). You must be heavily obscured or within full cover to try it at all.
Hide.description: Hidden on a Sneak total of {total}. A Search contests this with a fresh Perception check against a fresh Sneak check (pg 24); leaving full cover ends it (pg 127).

concealment.fullCover: Full cover (pg 127, 130 calls it total cover)
concealment.heavilyObscured: Heavily obscured — darkness, opaque fog, dense foliage (pg 118)
concealment.invisible: Invisible (pg 134: "for the purpose of hiding, the creature is heavily obscured")

Hide.dcPick: DC, used only when nothing is targeted ({count} targeted)
Hide.dialogHint: pg 127 sets the DC at "any nearby enemies passive sense scores" and then resolves it per enemy, so the creatures you have targeted are the real test and this field is the fallback for a patrol with no tokens. pg 127 requires heavy obscurement or full cover; pg 24's looser "if you have cover" is not followed, because taking it would leave pg 127's requirement doing nothing.
Hide.hidden: Hides ({ap} AP) — Sneak {total} vs DC {dc}: hidden.
Hide.failed: Hides ({ap} AP) — Sneak {total} vs DC {dc}: seen.
Hide.obscuredOnly: Hidden by obscurement rather than full cover — pg 127's "no longer within full cover" clause names cover only, so nothing here will end this automatically.
Hide.attackedHint: Attacking reveals you. The book never says so directly — it is established by the exception the Silencer mod carves out of it (pg 77), which is the only sentence in 136 pages about what attacking does to hiding.
Hide.silencedHint: Silencer (pg 77): the attack "does not reveal your presence to nearby creatures, allowing you to remain hidden except against the creature you attacked". Weapon mods are a bare text field in this system, so this is declared rather than detected.
Hide.lostCoverHint: pg 127: "If you are no longer within full cover of an enemy you are hidden from, you are no longer hidden."
Hide.obscuredNote: This hiding came from heavy obscurement, not full cover. pg 127's breaking clause only mentions cover, so nothing ends this on its own — call it at the table when the darkness goes.
Hide.revealedByAttack: Attacked from hiding, and so revealed (pg 77, by the exception the Silencer makes).
Hide.silenced: Attacked with a silenced weapon (pg 77): still hidden from everyone except the creature attacked.
Hide.lostCover: Out of full cover, and so no longer hidden (pg 127).
Hide.obscuredSurvives: Still hidden: this hiding came from heavy obscurement, and pg 127's breaking clause names full cover only.
Hide.needsConcealment: pg 127: "In order to hide you must be heavily obscured or within full cover." Half or three-quarters cover is not enough — pg 24's looser wording is not the rule this system follows.
Hide.noObservers: Hide's DC is the passive sense of nearby enemies (pg 127). Target the creatures you are hiding from, or give the dialog a DC.

Search.hint: 3 AP. An active Perception check to look for someone or something hidden (pg 127). Against a targeted creature who is hiding, it runs pg 24's contest: your Perception check against a fresh Sneak check from them.
Search.noQuarry: Nothing hidden was targeted, so there is no contest to run. pg 127 prints no DC for a Search — pg 21 draws the line instead: an active Perception check is your character deliberately looking, as against the passive sense that works unasked. The GM sets the bar.
Search.stillHidden: {target} stays hidden — Perception {searcher} against Sneak {hider}. The book addresses "their total is higher" and "your total is higher" and never a tie; a tie leaves the hider where they were.

Surprise.hint: Combat step 1 (pg 125). Compares the Sneak checks of anyone hiding against the passive sense of each creature on the opposing side — the creatures you have targeted. A recorded Hide supplies its total; otherwise a Sneak check is rolled here.
Surprise.description: Surprised (pg 125): no movement and no action on your first turn of combat, and no reaction until that turn ends. Passive sense {sense} missed the threat. Nothing here enforces the AP ban — this system gates no AP spending anywhere — but this marker is what makes you unaware for the pg 128 sneak attack.
Surprise.nobodyHiding: Nobody was hiding, so nobody is surprised: "If neither side tries to be stealthy, they automatically notice each other" (pg 125). Alert: {alert}.
Surprise.endHint: pg 125: the ban lasts your first turn of the combat, and the reaction ban "until that turn ends". Press this when it does — the window is a deadline about your own turn, and a Foundry duration would expire it silently.
Surprise.noSide: Target the creatures on the opposing side first. pg 125 compares the hiders' Sneak checks against "the passive sense score of each creature on the opposing side".

Dodge.hint: 6 AP. Until the start of your next turn, attacks against you have disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you may move 15 feet once in reaction to another creature's action, free (pg 126).
Dodge.description: Dodging (pg 126): attack rolls against you have disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you have one free {feet}-foot reactive move until the start of your next turn.
Dodge.descriptionLost: Dodging, with the benefit lost (pg 126): "You lose this benefit if you are dying or you cannot spend AP to move."
Dodge.started: Dodges ({ap} AP) — attacks against them have disadvantage while they can see the attacker, plus one free {feet}-foot reactive move (pg 126).
Dodge.lost: The benefit is lost: dying, or unable to spend AP to move (pg 126).
Dodge.state: Dodging — attackers roll at disadvantage if you can see them
Dodge.lostNote: The Dodge is doing nothing: pg 126 removes it while you are dying or cannot spend AP to move — that is Grappled (pg 134) or Restrained (pg 135). The 6 AP is spent regardless.
Dodge.moveHint: pg 126 grants one 15-foot reactive move before the start of your next turn, and prices no AP for it — three free 5-foot steps in a chapter where movement is 1 AP each.
Dodge.moved: Uses the Dodge's free {feet}-foot reactive move (pg 126).
Dodge.moveSpent: The Dodge's reactive move is "one time before the start of your next turn" (pg 126), and it has been used.
Dodge.endHint: The Dodge lasts "until the start of your next turn" (pg 126). Drop it there — the disadvantage it grants is declared by the attacker, so an effect that expired quietly would be worse than one a person clears.
Dodge.notDodging: Not dodging: the free reactive move comes with the Dodge action (pg 126).

Shove.title: Shove {target}
Shove.hint: 4 AP. Your Unarmed check against the target's Unarmed check or Agility check — their choice. Win and you knock them prone or push them 5 feet (pg 127). The last opposed roll left in the book, and the only one of the three without a "roll a 20" rider.
Shove.defensePick: The target's defence — the book gives them the choice
Shove.size: No more than one size larger than you (pg 127)
Shove.dialogHint: pg 127: "you make an Unarmed check contested by the target's Unarmed check or Agility check (the target chooses the ability to use)". Those are two different quantities — a skill bonus and a raw ability modifier — and the larger of the two is pre-selected so a target prompted on somebody else's turn is not defended badly by default. Reach and size are declared: this system measures no distance, and nothing in it or in the book records a size for a player character.
Shove.pushed: {target} is pushed {feet} feet — {shover} against {defender}. The token is not moved: which direction 5 feet goes is the map's answer, not the sheet's.
Shove.failed: {target} holds their ground — {shover} against {defender}. You must win the contest (pg 127), so a tie is a loss for the shover, and there is no raw-20 rider here as there is on Grapple and Escape.
Shove.noTarget: Target the creature you are shoving first (pg 127).
Shove.refused: pg 127 requires the target to be within your reach and no more than one size larger than you.

TakeCover.hint: 3 AP. From three-quarters or half cover, squat, kneel, or duck into full cover (pg 127). Full cover cannot be targeted directly by an attack at all (pg 130).
TakeCover.description: Full cover, taken (pg 127). A target in full cover "can't be targeted directly by an attack" (pg 130) — declare total cover on the attack. Attacking ends it.
TakeCover.took: Takes cover ({ap} AP) — from {from} into full cover (pg 127). Attacks against them should now be declared as total cover, which refuses outright.
TakeCover.leaveHint: pg 127: "If you attack while taking cover, you no longer have full cover."
TakeCover.left: Attacked from cover, so no longer in full cover (pg 127).
TakeCover.needsPartial: pg 127 gates Take Cover on having "only three quarters or half cover". With no cover there is nothing to duck into, and full cover is already the outcome.

Stand.hint: 5 AP to stand up from prone (pg 126). pg 135: a prone creature's only movement option is to crawl, unless it stands up and thereby ends the condition.
Stand.stood: Stands up from prone ({ap} AP, pg 126).
Stand.notProne: Not prone, so there is nothing to stand up from.

Stow.hint: 3 AP: "You take a weapon you are holding and put it into your inventory" (pg 127).
Stow.notHeld: That weapon is not in hand, so there is nothing to stow.

Equip.hint: 3 AP: "You take a weapon within reach and prepare to attack with it with any hands you have free" (pg 126). The drop clause is reported, not enforced — there is no hands resource in this system or in the book.
Equip.wouldDrop: pg 126 would drop these on the ground: {weapons}. Not enforced — the sentence needs to know which hands are free, and 136 pages never say how many hands a creature has or that a Two Handed weapon occupies two. The same gap leaves the v2.1 free-hand reload requirement reported rather than checked.
Equip.alreadyHeld: That weapon is already in hand.

Backgrounds.title: Background
Backgrounds.pickHint: Every background grants +2 to three skills, one trait, and a starting kit that differs by race (pg 13-18). The kit shown is the one printed for this character's race; the Apply button's tooltip is the printed sentence it came from. Applying is a one-time act — it refuses while a background is already applied, and Clear takes it back.
Backgrounds.clearHint: Reverses exactly what applying wrote: the skill points and caps it added, and the documents it created that are still on this sheet. Anything since eaten, sold or deleted is simply reported as gone.
Backgrounds.clearNote: Cleared items are the ones this button created and no others; a stack you have added to is not touched.
Backgrounds.itemsStillHeld: granted items still on the sheet
Backgrounds.customNote: Choose three skills and a kit yourself (850 caps, pg 13)
Backgrounds.noKitHint: The chapter prints a kit for each of Human, Ghoul, Gen-2 Synth, Robot and Super Mutant. This character's race field holds something else, so there is nothing to apply — set the race first.
Backgrounds.raceChanged: This background was applied for a different race, so the kit on the sheet is not the one this character's race prints.
Backgrounds.alreadyApplied: A background is already applied to this character. Clear it first — applying a second one would stack three more +2s and a second kit onto a sheet that has been played since.
Backgrounds.nothingApplied: No background has been applied to this character, so there is nothing to clear. A background typed into the field by hand is not a ledger and cannot be reversed.
Backgrounds.noKitForRace: The chapter prints no starting kit for the race "{race}" (pg 13-18). Set the character's race to Human, Ghoul, Gen-2 Synth, Robot or Super Mutant first.
Backgrounds.cardTraitMissing: Trait: {trait} — not found in the Perks and Traits compendium, so it was not granted. Add it by hand.
Backgrounds.cardReported: Reported rather than granted: {entries}. The book leaves these to the table — a model the player picks, or an item its own tables never print.
Backgrounds.cardMissing: Not in the equipment compendium: {entries}. Add them by hand.
Backgrounds.cardCleared: Background cleared: {name}. {items} item(s) removed, {caps} caps handed back, and the skill points reversed.
Backgrounds.cardGone: {count} granted item(s) were already gone from the sheet and could not be removed.

Decay.bulky: Bulky adds a level of decay (now {levels}).

RobotType.label: Robot Type
RobotType.hint: Handy, Protectron, and Robobrain differ in body plan: which limbs a targeted attack can name, what each costs in AP, and what can be severed (pg 9-11).

handy.limbs: Three arms, three eyes, a core, and a jet engine. No head, groin, or legs to target or sever. Targeted attacks to the eyes cost 2 less AP; the jet engine works like a leg but costs 2 more.
handy.jetEngine: Jet Engine: hovers while active and moving, triggering no floor-based traps or activated effects. Falls to the ground when knocked prone, stunned, or unconscious.

protectron.limbs: Two arms, two legs, two hands, two feet, a head, and a torso. No eyes or groin to target or sever.
protectron.reinforcedPlating: Reinforced Plating: damage threshold increased by 1, even without armor.
protectron.slow: Slow: at most {ap} AP may be spent on movement per turn.

robobrain.limbs: Two arms, two hands, a head, a torso, and all terrain rollers. No legs, feet, eyes, or groin to target or sever. The rollers work like legs but cannot be severed.
robobrain.allTerrainRollers: All Terrain Rollers: no extra AP to move through difficult terrain.
robobrain.neuroTransmitters: NeuroTransmitters: vulnerable to electricity damage, and a targeted attack to the head that deals damage inflicts two conditions instead of one.

Robots.severedLimbs: A severed limb causes no shock and is reattached with 3 steel and 1 circuitry.
Robots.reattachMinutes: Reattaching a limb takes {minutes} minutes (10 − crafting bonus).
Robots.reattachAp: Crafting bonus covers the whole time — reattaching a limb costs {ap} AP instead.
Robots.slowExceeded: Slow (pg 10): this move alone costs {ap} AP, past the {cap} AP a Protectron may spend on movement during a turn. Reported, not enforced — nothing in this system deducts AP, and nothing totals what a turn has spent on moving.
Robots.rollersSprint: All Terrain Rollers waives the extra AP difficult terrain charges (pg 116); a sprint is not surcharged by difficult terrain, it is ended by it (pg 117). So the trait takes nothing off here and this run still stops.
Robots.rollersTravel: Over a day's travel, difficult terrain divides the distance covered rather than charging AP (pg 116), so All Terrain Rollers takes nothing off this leg either.
Robots.neuroCondition: NeuroTransmitters (pg 11): a targeted attack to a Robobrain's head inflicts two conditions instead of one — this is roll {index} of {count}.
Robots.reattachHint: Bolt a robot's severed limb back on (pg 11): 3 steel and 1 circuitry, and 10 minutes less your Crafting bonus — or 6 AP once that reaches zero. Target the robot first. Nothing is consumed and no AP is deducted.
Robots.reattachJunk: {steel} steel and {circuitry} circuitry junk — reported, not consumed: this system has no junk documents to spend.
Robots.reattachWhose: Using {mechanic}'s Crafting bonus of {bonus} against the printed {base} minutes. The book allows "their or your" bonus (pg 11) and never says which — this uses whoever pressed the button, so a robot doing its own repairs targets itself.
Robots.reattachReported: A severed limb is narrated rather than tracked: nothing here checks that a limb is missing, and nothing puts one back. The price is the whole of what the book prints.
Robots.reattachNotRobot: {name} is not a robot. The severed-limb clause is printed in the Robot entry (pg 11); a limb that was never bolted on is not reattached with circuitry.
Robots.fuelNotARobot: Only a robot has a tank or a chassis to fill (pg 10).
Robots.fuelFilled: Tank filled: {ap} AP, with a gallon of fuel or {junk} oil junk items (pg 10). The oil is consumed from this machine's junk when held; the gallon alternative is not automated. If this machine was unconscious from running dry, it wakes.
Robots.fuelCoreLoaded: Fusion core loaded into the chassis: {days} days of operation without fuel (pg 10).
Robots.fuelOverdue: Running dry: {hours} hour(s) past the {limit}-hour tank (pg 10) — one Endurance check per hour, DC rising 2 per success.
Robots.fuelUnconscious: The machine falls unconscious until another creature fills its tank (pg 10).
Robots.fuelGallonPaid: Paid with the gallon of fuel — declared, not consumed: whether the Flamer's Fuel ammo is the same fuel is the table's call.
Robots.faultyNotFaulty: {program} is not faulty on this machine — nothing to clear (pg 90).
Robots.faultyCheck: Clearing faulty programming: {program} — {circuitry} circuitry and a DC {dc} Crafting check (pg 90)
Robots.faultyCleared: The programming is no longer faulty: {program} is cleared. The {circuitry} circuitry is spent.
Robots.faultyFailed: The repair fails: {program} stays faulty, and the {circuitry} circuitry is lost anyway — the book spends it either way (pg 90).

Vision.title: Vision & Fire
Vision.sensesHint: Both are pg 119, and the book gives neither a default radius — it says "within a specific radius" and "within a specified range" and leaves the number to whatever granted the sense. 0 means the creature does not have it. These are stored as an actor flag rather than a schema field, so no Active Effect can grant them yet; promoting them to system data is an outstanding integration point.
Vision.reportHint: Post this line to chat, so everyone is working from the same answer.
Vision.bandObscured: The weather in force leaves everything past {feet} ft lightly obscured (pg 121-123).
Vision.bandBlind: The weather in force leaves you effectively Blinded past {feet} ft (pg 121-123).
Vision.setLightHint: Set the scene's illumination (pg 118-119) and paint it onto the canvas: bright is globally lit, dim is globally lit at dim intensity — which is exactly "dim light creates a lightly obscured area" — and darkness switches global light off so only placed lights and token vision reach anything.
Vision.cutoffsOn: In force — tokens are carrying this system's overrides.
Vision.cutoffsOff: Not applied — every token sees with the vision it was authored with.
Vision.applyHint: Cap every token's sight range on this scene from the light level and whatever distance bands the weather imposes (pg 118-123). Each token's own blindsight and nightvision are taken into account, so one press gives every creature a different answer. Their authored vision is snapshotted first, so Clear is exact.
Vision.clearHint: Put every token's vision back exactly as it was authored, deleting the detection modes this system added so core recomputes its own defaults.
Vision.nothingToClear: No token on this scene is carrying a vision override.
Vision.cutoffsNote: Applies to every token on the scene, not to your target — the light and the weather do not pick favourites, and each token's cutoff is computed from its own senses. Nothing re-applies itself: change the light or the weather and press Apply again.
Vision.igniteHint: Light a fire on the targeted token's square (pg 118). The book never says how big a newly lit area is — a flamer, an incendiary grenade and a dropped flare plainly differ — and it hands the spread rate to the GM outright ("factors that could allow flames to spread slower, such as winds, rain, or if the flames are surrounded by non-flammable objects"), so both are asked for rather than assumed.
Vision.pickOne: Target exactly one token to mark where the fire starts.
Vision.noOrigin: That target has no position this system can read, so there is nowhere to light the fire. Target a token placed on the canvas.
Vision.spreadHint: Grow every fire on the scene by its spread rate (pg 118). Pressed by a GM rather than run off the combat round, because the book says the rate is the GM's: "The spread of the flames is up to GM's discretion."
Vision.burnHint: Every creature standing in a fire takes its damage and gains Burning (pg 118). Once per press per creature: the book names two triggers — moving through and starting a turn in it — and never says a creature that does both is charged twice, so how often this is pressed is the GM's call.
Vision.burningAp: Burning (pg 133): a burning creature takes 1d10 fire damage at the start of its turns, and can spend {ap} AP to put itself out. The AP is reported, never deducted — spend it by hand.
Vision.extinguishHint: Put this fire out (pg 118). The book names water, cryo damage and a fire extinguisher, and gives no DC, no quantity and no action cost for any of the three, so nothing is rolled.
Vision.extinguishAllHint: Put every fire on the scene out at once, by the chosen means.
Vision.noFires: Nothing is burning on this scene.
Vision.gmOnly: Only the GM can change the scene's light or its fires.
Vision.gmNote: These controls write the scene, not your character, so only a GM sees them. Nothing here happens on its own — no hook advances a fire, re-applies a cutoff or re-lights the canvas.
Vision.fireMeta: {radius} ft from the origin, {formula} fire damage and Burning, spreading {spread} ft each round — burning for {rounds} round(s) so far (pg 118).
Vision.fireNextDie: Gains another 1d10 in {rounds} round(s): the damage climbs by 1d10 for every 20 ft the area grows outward (pg 118).
Vision.fireAtMaximum: At the printed ceiling of 50d10 (pg 118). It can still spread; the damage no longer climbs.
Vision.fireNotSpreading: Not spreading, so the damage will never climb — the rate is the GM's to set: "There are factors that could allow flames to spread slower, such as winds, rain, or if the flames are surrounded by non-flammable objects" (pg 118).

StealthField.description: Invisible, along with everything you are carrying, for 1 minute (pg 12).
StealthField.raised: Raises the Stealth Field ({ap} AP) — invisible, and everything they carry with them, for {seconds} seconds.
StealthField.freeUse: First use today: no Perception cost.
StealthField.decayed: Use {use} today — Perception drops by {lost} for {hours} hours (now {score}). Each reduction runs its own 24-hour clock.
StealthField.atFloor: Perception is at the printed minimum of 1 — further uses cost nothing more, and no perk requirement is affected.
StealthField.perksUnaffected: This reduction does not limit using or choosing perks with a Perception requirement (pg 12).
StealthField.decayDescription: −1 Perception for {hours} hours, from a repeat use of the Stealth Field (pg 12).
StealthField.ended: Drops the Stealth Field — no longer invisible.
StealthField.already: The Stealth Field is already up. Raising it again would spend a second use on a minute that is already running.
StealthField.needsNightkin: Only a Nightkin Super Mutant has the Stealth Field (pg 12) — set the variant on the sheet first.
StealthField.hint: 3 AP. You and everything you carry turn invisible for 1 minute. Every use after the first each day costs 1 Perception for 24 hours, to a minimum of 1 — which never disqualifies a Perception-gated perk.
StealthField.active: Stealth Field up — click to drop

MutantVariant.label: Variant Trait
MutantVariant.hint: GM-optional (pg 12). A variant REPLACES Superior Strength — it never stacks with it. Bulky is unaffected either way.

descriptions.superiorStrength: Superior Strength: Strength increases by 1 and cannot be lower than 6; Carry Load increased by 40 (pg 11).
descriptions.defectiveStrain: Defective Strain: Strength and Endurance both increase by 2 and Carry Load is increased by 40; Intelligence is reduced by 2 and cannot be raised higher than 3. No Strength floor — that belonged to the trait this replaces (pg 12).
descriptions.nightkin: Nightkin: Strength increases by 1 and cannot be lower than 6; Carry Load increased by 40; and you gain the Stealth Field (pg 12).

Junk.missing: Materials not spent, because they are not on this sheet: {materials}. The action went ahead anyway — this system reports a cost it cannot verify rather than blocking a rule (as it does with AP and with every distance in feet). Spend them from paper if that is where your junk lives, or import the stacks from the equipment compendium (they are named “Junk: …”) to have them spent for you.
Junk.typeHint: Which crafting material this stack is (steel, cloth, oil, …). Leave empty for gear that is not junk. Free text so homebrew materials work; shipped names are matched loosely.
Junk.recipeDeferred: The recipe prints an "or", so nothing was spent: the book offers a choice and this system will not pick a branch for you. Deduct whichever you used.
Junk.recipeUnstocked: Not spent because this system ships no document for them — the book names specific found objects rather than stocked materials: {materials}. That is expected, not a shortfall.
Junk.recipeUncountable: Lines nothing can count, left to the table: {materials}

Mods.silencerFromWeapon: [Silencer fitted (pg 77) — this attack does not give your position away]
Mods.label: Weapon modifications
Mods.hint: Ranged weapons have 6 mod slots and cease function past them (pg 75). Melee weapons take one modification at a time, switchable in 5 minutes unless the mod says it is permanent (pg 65).
Mods.slotsExceeded: Mod slots {used} of {limit} — this weapon ceases function (pg 75).
Mods.detached: Takes the {mod} off {weapon} (pg {page}). The modification goes back into the pack — the row prints a time to unequip as well as to equip, and the Lucky Charm says outright that a charm can be moved between weapons.
Mods.swapAp: Time to fit or remove: {ap} AP, which is how this row prices it rather than in minutes. Reported, never deducted.
Mods.swapMinutes: {minutes} minute(s) to attach or remove, at Intelligence {intelligence}.
Mods.swapNever: The row prints "N/A" for the time to equip or unequip, so the book gives no procedure for moving this one — the table decides.
Mods.costPercent: {percent}% of the weapon's base cost ({caps} caps here).

automation.partial: Partly automated — see the mod's note
automation.text: Not automated: the printed text applies, this system does not enforce it.
automation.derived: Computed on the weapon — the modified numbers are shown here; the roll and carry-load still read the printed row until each switches over.

ineligible.category: The book prints this in the {category} modification table.
ineligible.weaponType: The Equippable Weapons column does not list this kind of weapon.
ineligible.excludedWeapon: The Equippable Weapons column excludes the {name}.
ineligible.requiresProperty: This mod needs a weapon with {property}.
ineligible.forbidsProperty: This mod does not fit a weapon with {property}.
ineligible.slots: {used} mod slots — past the {limit} a ranged weapon has (pg 75).
ineligible.meleeLimit: This melee weapon already carries its one modification (pg 65).
ineligible.advisory: The book does not print this combination. Attach it anyway if that is the call at your table — nothing here refuses.

Mods.scopeClose: [{mod} (pg {page}) — the target is {distance} ft away, within its {feet} ft: disadvantage]
Mods.capacitorSpent: [{mod} (pg 75-76) — {rounds} rounds spent instead of 1 for +{damage} damage; {loaded} left in the magazine. Hold the boost for the damage roll too]
Mods.capacitorDamage: [{mod} — +{damage} damage for the {rounds} rounds the attack spent]
Mods.capacitorDry: {weapon} needs {rounds} rounds for the {mod} and has {loaded} — reload, or attack without the boost
Mods.capacitorNoMagazine: [{mod} — no magazine is tracked for this weapon, so its {rounds} rounds cannot be spent and the damage is not increased]
Mods.upgraded: [Upgraded (pg 65) — {count} damage die/dice rolled a 1 or a 2: +{bonus}, for {total} in all. Read once per qualifying die, as Weighted and Destructive read the same phrase]
Mods.luckyCharmRuling: "Each player character can only benefit from one lucky charm" (pg 76). Nothing here refuses the attachment and nothing picks a winner — the book forbids the arrangement without saying which charm works, so decide at the table which weapon is the charmed one. Every charmed weapon still shows its printed −1 critical hit chance until you take one off.
Mods.grantedHint: The printed special column is never rewritten — these are merged on top of it on read, so "if the weapon already has …" (Hardened Receiver, Laser Sight) can still be answered against what the weapon came with.
Mods.grantedAlready: {weapon} already prints {property}, so this modification's "if it already has {property}" clause is the one that applies — and that clause is not automated.
Mods.grantedSemiAutomatic: Semi-Automatic is granted and parsed, but its benefit is priced in AP and nothing in this system spends AP yet (BACKLOG E1). The property is on the weapon; the free attack is still the table's to run.
Mods.grantedDefensive: Defensive is live: blocking while holding this weapon adds {dt} to your damage threshold (pg 61, 70, 127).
Mods.reloadAlternativeHint: A choice, not a discount: the printed reload still applies. Every revolver in the book has Manual Reload, so the decision is 3 AP for three rounds or {ap} AP for the whole cylinder.
Mods.infraredNormal: {target} can be targeted with an ordinary attack.
Mods.infraredDisadvantaged: {target} is invisible: attack rolls against them have disadvantage (pg 134). An Infrared Scope would read through it (pg 76).
Mods.infraredBlind: {target} is heavily obscured: this is a blind attack (pg 128) — Luck modifier instead of your skill bonus, against a DC instead of their AC. An Infrared Scope would read through it (pg 76).
Mods.infraredRefused: {target} is behind full cover and cannot be targeted directly (pg 130) — the Infrared Scope's own clause stops there too (pg 76).
Mods.infraredDc: Blind attack DC {dc}, at {distance} ft (pg 128). Not rolled here: the Luck substitution is unbuilt, so run it at the table.
Mods.infraredDcUnstated: The blind attack DC is 5 + the distance in feet, rounded down in 5s (pg 128) — declare a distance to see the number.
Mods.infraredStillHidden: Targeting, not seeing: {target} is still hidden, still needs a Search to find (pg 24), and still has advantage attacking back.
Mods.markNeedsMod: This weapon has no On-Board Target Tracking modification to mark with (pg 76).
Mods.markOutOfRange: {target} is {distance} ft away, past this weapon's {range} ft short range — nothing to mark (pg 76).
Mods.marked: Marks {target} with {weapon} — {ap} AP (pg 76). Attack rolls against {target} have advantage.
Mods.markDuration: The book prints no duration: ruled spent by the first attack roll made against {target}, by anyone.
Mods.markRangeUnstated: Short range is {range} ft; no distance was declared, so "within the weapon's short range" is the table's call.
Mods.markDescription: Marked by {by}'s On-Board Target Tracking (pg 76). Attack rolls against this creature have advantage until one is made.
Mods.markNotOwned: Marking writes to {target}'s own sheet, and you do not own it — ask the GM to place the mark.
Mods.markNotCleared: The mark on {target} was spent by this attack, but only {target}'s owner can clear it — a GM should drop the Marked effect.
Mods.markedTarget: [Marked (pg 76) — advantage, and the mark is spent]
Mods.markedNoAdvantage: [Marked (pg 76) — the mark is spent, but this roll was declared with advantage or disadvantage, so it granted nothing]

derived.label: With modifications
derived.hint: What this weapon's row becomes once its modifications are folded in. The printed row above is left exactly as the book prints it.
derived.unchanged: No modification changes this weapon's numbers.

choice.label: {mod}: which increase?
choice.hint: The book prints this as an either/or and gives no default, so nothing is applied until you pick one (pg 65, 76).

note.pendingChoice: {mod} prints "critical hit modifier or damage dice increases by 1" — pick one; neither applies until you do.
note.notPrinted: {mod} would change this weapon's {stat}, and the book prints none for this weapon.
note.offLadder: {damage} has no damage die to step (the ranks are d4, d6, d8, d10, d12), so the rank change does not apply.
note.noCritModifier: The printed Critical Hit column ({crit}) is not a multiplier, so there is nothing for the critical hit modifier to increase — take the damage die instead.

bounded.apCost: A printed AP minimum or maximum took part of the change.
bounded.damage: The damage die is already at the end of the rank ladder (minimum d4, maximum d12).

Mods.swapTime: Time to fit or remove: {minutes} minutes, after the Intelligence discount the row prints. Reported, never spent.
Mods.documentSpent: One {mod} was spent from the pack.
Mods.documentMissing: No {mod} was in the pack, so nothing was spent — attached anyway, and the shortfall is reported rather than blocking (the same terms junk and materials are on).
Mods.ceasesFunction: This weapon has ceased to function: its mod slot total is greater than 6 (pg 75). Reported rather than refused, because the book describes it as a state the weapon reaches, not a fitting it forbids.
Mods.choicePending: The {mod} prints an "or" nobody has answered yet — pick which benefit it gives on the weapon's own sheet.
Mods.advisory: These are advisory. The melee table hands eligibility to the GM outright, so nothing here refuses an attachment — it says which printed clauses this weapon does not satisfy.
Mods.whyWeaponType: The Equippable Weapons column admits no clause this weapon satisfies.
Mods.whyExcluded: The column names {name} in its "except for" list.
Mods.whyRequiresProperty: The row requires the {property} property, which this weapon does not print.
Mods.whyForbidsProperty: The row forbids the {property} property, which this weapon prints.
Mods.whyRequiresMod: The row requires the {mod} to be fitted first.
Mods.whyConflict: The row cannot share a weapon with the {mod}.
Mods.whySlots: Fitting it puts the weapon at {used} mod slots, past the printed {limit}.
Mods.whyMeleeLimit: Melee weapons can only have one modification (pg 65).

Mods.needsOwner: A modification is fitted from a character's sheet: the crafted part is spent out of their pack and the fitting time reads their Intelligence. Drag the weapon onto an actor first.
Mods.panelHint: Every printed modification is listed. A bullet marks one whose Equippable Weapons column this weapon does not satisfy — it can still be fitted, because the melee table hands that question to the GM outright, and the card will say which clauses it fails.
Mods.choicesPendingPanel: A fitted modification prints an "or" nobody has answered. Until one is picked the weapon keeps its printed number.

ShortCircuit.rerouted: Re-routes and resets the circuit — {ap} AP (pg 135), reported not deducted. One level removed; {levels} remaining.
ShortCircuit.none: {name} has no levels of Short Circuit to re-route.
ShortCircuit.wet: Wet while short-circuiting (pg 135): the levels double, {before} → {after}.
ShortCircuit.healed: Healed to full hit points, so all {levels} level(s) of Short Circuit are removed (pg 135).
